title: settlement_loop correctness hardening (pre-wiring keystone) — review-team-3 cluster
description: review-team-3 (w96w45naz) confirmed 5 defects in hermes_quant/daemon/settlement_loop.py, the BMA-Beta-auto-learning keystone (ADR-0083). All LATENT (no production caller — daemon/main.py uses construct_realized_outcomes/dispatch_settlement, not join_exit_fills), not Monday-blocking, but must be correct BEFORE wiring into dispatch. (1) HIGH: join_exit_fills reads synthetic schema (rec['side']/['qty']/['asof']) incompatible with the real bus from PaperReactor._record_to_dict (asof_decision/asof_execution, target_position_pct/fill_size_pct, NO side/qty/exec_id) — a real entry+exit pair settles to ([],{}); docstring 'reads the SAME records' is false. Fix: bus->lot adapter (side from sign of target_position_pct/fill_size_pct delta, qty from |delta|, asof from asof_execution); correct docstring; real-_record_to_dict-shaped test. (2) MED: same-asof entry/exit matched in reverse (exec_id lexical tie-break) inverts side+magnitude. Fix: tie-break by positional bus index/proposal lineage, opening before closing. (3) MED: out-of-order carry-in opens a phantom opposing lot, violating one-direction-per-queue. Fix: defer the exit on the lot.asof>asof break instead of opening a residual lot; assert invariant. (4) LOW: mixed tz-aware/naive asof across carry-in raises TypeError; normalize to UTC in _coerce_asof. (5) LOW: compute_horizon_return fee (fees/ep) diverges from join_exit_fills (fees/(ep*qty)) for qty!=1; add qty param. Each fix->adversarial-verify, offline-deterministic, additive (keystone stays unwired), asof-honest.

title: Unify position-unit basis before Option-E: state.db (shares), settlement FIFO (NAV-fraction), and reconstruct (paper-filtered) cannot agree on det-equity net
description: The keystone acceptance gate of the whole rearchitecture (ADR-0091:365) demands three folds 'report the SAME net' for det-equity AAPL, but the three folds track that net in three incompatible regimes: 33.33 shares (state.db), ~0.05 NAV-fraction (settlement FIFO), and dropped-or-fractional (reconstruct's default reactor_filter='paper'). A single shared carry-forward normalizer carrying ONE running_net per (account, asset_class, asset) bucket cannot reconcile mixed shares-and-NAV-fraction inputs in one bucket — subtracting 0.05 from a 33.33 running_net is unit-incoherent. The increment-0 §0.2 scope acknowledges both paths exist but specifies no unit-unification, so the gate as written is unsatisfiable against current code. Existing seed ra01 covers delta-vs-latest-target divergence, NOT this shares-vs-NAV-fraction unit mismatch. || EVIDENCE: docs/adr/ADR-0091-reactors-emit-traded-delta.md:365 — PARITY gate requires state/portfolio_state.py rebuild AND daemon/settlement_loop.py FIFO AND portfolio/state.py::reconstruct_portfolio_state to 'all report the SAME net for the AAPL/BA fixtures' ; hermes_quant/react/deterministic_equity.py:373,385 — SAME record carries fill_size_pct=realized_fill_pct (NAV-fraction ~0.05) AND reactor_metadata['quantity']=filled_qty (TRUE shares ~33.33) ; hermes_quant/state/portfolio_state.py:982-984,998 — det-equity fold uses pos_delta=float(leg_quantity)=shares; new_qty=old_qty+pos_delta — so get_positions().quantity is true shares on this path ; hermes_quant/daemon/settlement_loop.py:524 — FIFO reads fill_size_pct as the lot qty (NAV-fraction), never reads reactor_metadata.quantity — so the same AAPL net is tracked as ~0.05 NAV-fraction in the settlement view ; hermes_quant/risk/portfolio_normalize.py:101-106 — PortfolioState.positions documented as 'symbol -> signed target_position_pct of NAV'; gross_exposure_pct=sum(abs(p)) assumes NAV-fraction units ; docs/plans/2026-06-12-increment-0-scope.md:34-38 — the §0.2 normalizer is keyed (account_id, asset_class, asset) with ONE running_net per bucket and must 'handle BOTH the fill_size_pct path AND the reactor_metadata.quantity path' — but never specifies how to reconcile a single bucket carrying both unit regimes || FOLDED into Increment 0 (subsumes the unit-unification; the Option-E PARITY gate precondition). Tracked in increment-0-scope §0.2.

title: Fix portfolio-cap clip reading true shares as NAV-fraction on the deterministic-equity/HITL path (live cap bypass or false silence)
description: The portfolio-cap is the live safety band-aid against the exact gross-exposure-runaway failure mode of INCIDENT-2026-06-02. On the deterministic-equity/HITL money path the cap reads true-share counts as NAV-fractions, producing two live failure modes: (1) adding to an existing position is unbounded because the de-risking guard always sees shares >> the new fraction and skips the clip; (2) opening any new name while another equity position is open is falsely silenced because held shares inflate gross to thousands of percent. The paper-default book is shared between NAV-fraction PaperReactor and true-share DeterministicEquityReactor, so the book is unit-mixed and the cap math is wrong whenever any share-denominated position is present. ADR-0086/0087 documented the intended fix but deferred it behind the very migration that already shipped. Distinct from the known cap-bypass seed (that one is the env-flag gate; this is a unit-confusion arithmetic bug). || EVIDENCE: hermes_quant/react/paper.py:447-450 — _portfolio_cap_clip builds pos_map[symbol]=position.quantity with stale comment 'Positions are stored as NAV-fraction quantities in v0.1 (ADR-0041)' ; hermes_quant/state/portfolio_state.py:707-733 — get_positions returns quantity=float(row['quantity']) raw, no qty×mark/equity conversion ; hermes_quant/state/portfolio_state.py:982-984 — det-equity fold stores pos_delta=float(leg_quantity)=TRUE SHARES, so quantity on this path is shares not a NAV fraction ; hermes_quant/react/paper.py:463-465 — de-risking guard: existing=pos_map.get(symbol); if abs(fill_size_pct) <= abs(existing)+1e-9: return None (skip clip). With existing=100 shares and fill_size_pct=0.05 the guard is True -> cap fully BYPASSED when adding to a held position ; hermes_quant/risk/portfolio_normalize.py:101-106 — PortfolioCaps.standard gross cap is on sum(abs(NAV-fraction)); a 100-share held position inflates gross to 10000% -> any new name's headroom is negative -> fire clipped to ~0 and silenced (false silence) ; docs/FLAGS.md:50-51 — HERMES_QUANT_PORTFOLIO_CAPS (armed) and HERMES_QUANT_DETERMINISTIC_EQUITY ('Just flipped' 2026-06-05) are both LIVE ; docs/adr/ADR-0087 / ADR-0086 acknowledge the fix in principle ('derive position_pct = qty × mark / equity, not raw quantity') but defer it 'with the share migration' — the det-equity share migration already shipped and flipped on || FOLDED into Increment 0: not safely hot-patchable (needs mark-injection seam; no per-row unit discriminator). Operator mitigation in docs/operations/2026-06-13-operator-action-packet.md A1. Justified deferral.

title: Guard NaN spot/nav/greeks in options_gate cap checks (NaN gamma/vega/net-delta passes the cap silently — fail-open)
description: A NaN spot (zero-length bar / stale feed) or a NaN greek from a pricing-model edge case (ATM DTE=0, IV overflow in the GBS kernel) produces NaN gamma_dollar / net-delta. 'NaN > threshold' is always False, so the gamma, vega, and net-delta caps all pass NaN silently — the canonical NaN-fail-open class. The None-only check in aggregate_net_greeks lets NaN through without the GreekComputationError silence path. The equity-side gate already has the isfinite pattern; the options gate is missing it. Merged from two candidates (the spot/nav cap-input gap and the aggregate_net_greeks None-vs-NaN gap) since they are the same fail-open class on the same gate. || EVIDENCE: hermes_quant/risk/options_gate.py:616-617 — gamma_dollar = abs(portfolio_after.gamma*spot*spot); if gamma_dollar > cap*nav — no math.isfinite(spot) or isfinite(nav) check before this ; hermes_quant/risk/options_gate.py:643 — net-delta cap: if abs(portfolio_after.delta*spot) > cap*nav — also unchecked for NaN spot/nav ; hermes_quant/risk/options_gate.py:596 — only max_loss has an isfinite guard; spot and nav are not guarded ; hermes_quant/options/data.py:276-279 — aggregate_net_greeks raises GreekComputationError only when a greek is None; does NOT check math.isfinite, so NaN greeks propagate into candidate_net ; hermes_quant/risk/options_gate.py:512-520 — gate only catches GreekComputationError to silence; NaN greeks never trigger that path ; tests/unit/test_options_gate.py — 0 matches for nan/NaN/isfinite/isnan (no NaN input tests for spot, nav, or greeks) ; hermes_quant/risk/gate.py:536-537 — DefaultRiskGate checks isfinite on drawdown_pct; options_gate lacks this pattern || FIXED commit 6e17488 (TDD, 90/90, ruff clean): isfinite guard on spot/nav + non-finite greek fail-closed.

title: Wire realized-outcome settlement into daemon/main.py: side/asof field mismatch makes per-tick settlement a permanent zero-outcome no-op
description: Two compounding defects on the same daemon settlement path: (1) construct_realized_outcomes keys off 'side'/'asof' fields that the real execution bus never emits, so every actual fill is dropped at the else:continue and the loop constructs zero RealizedOutcome/EpisodeOutcome — a dead measurement instrument logging n_realized:0; (2) the schema-correct join_exit_fills (the ADR-0083 horizon-return accounting that feeds BMA learning and the locked-in-loss rail) is never wired into the daemon at all. Net effect: if daemon/main.py is ever the active loop, the system makes repeated sizing decisions with calibrators that receive zero outcome feedback and learns nothing. Merged the two candidates (zero-outcomes field mismatch + join_exit_fills not wired) since both are the same dead-settlement-on-daemon-path root. || EVIDENCE: hermes_quant/react/paper.py:35-55 — _record_to_dict emits {fill_size_pct, asof_execution, ...} with NO 'side' key and NO 'asof' key (emits asof_execution) ; hermes_quant/daemon/settlement_loop.py:141,146-151 — side=exec_rec.get('side'); if side=='buy' ... elif side=='sell' ... else: continue — real bus has no 'side', so every fill hits the else and is dropped ; hermes_quant/daemon/settlement_loop.py:183 — pd.Timestamp(exec_rec['asof']) — real bus has no 'asof' (it has asof_execution), KeyError-equivalent path ; hermes_quant/daemon/main.py:51-52,232,234 — daemon imports and calls construct_realized_outcomes + dispatch_settlement on raw bus records; these v0.1.1 funcs were never migrated to the bus schema ; hermes_quant/daemon/settlement_loop.py:377-382 — comment: join_exit_fills (the schema-correct exit-join) has 'NO production caller yet (daemon/main.py wires construct_realized_outcomes + dispatch_settlement, not join_exit_fills)' ; hermes_quant/autonomous.py:280,296 — only caller of join_exit_fills is the kill-switch cumulative-PnL rail, NOT the calibrator/learning path || RESOLVED-BY-DELETION f998369: daemon/main.py (which wired the dead construct_realized_outcomes settlement) was deleted. The dead code no longer exists.

title: Make portfolio-cap clip atomic under concurrent fire: position read sits outside the append_locked critical section
description:
Two concurrent PaperReactor.execute() calls (autonomous-tick firing multiple symbols) both read the same pre-fill position state, both see headroom, both pass the cap, and both append fills that together exceed the gross-exposure cap. The ADR-0091 resolution explicitly names this non-atomicity as the reason Option B was rejected, yet the live producer still has it and there is no test asserting the cap holds under concurrent fire. Distinct from the cap-unit-confusion item (that is an arithmetic bug; this is a TOCTOU race). || EVIDENCE: hermes_quant/react/paper.py:438,445 — _portfolio_cap_clip reads get_portfolio_state().get_positions() at the start of execute(), well before the bus write ; hermes_quant/react/paper.py:291 — append_locked(self.executions_path) is the write-lock boundary; the cap check happens before this, outside the flock ; docs/adr/ADR-0091-reactors-emit-traded-delta.md:39-43 — Option B was rejected precisely because 'paper.py position read sits OUTSIDE the append_locked block (:291), so producer read-compute-append is non-atomic' ; hermes_quant/risk/portfolio_normalize.py:406-412 — clip_one_to_remaining_headroom takes a read-only snapshot with no locking or post-compute re-verification || RED PROOF LANDED 2026-06-13 (workflow wt13usy0p): tests/unit/test_portfolio_cap_cross_symbol_race.py multiprocessing proof (fork + Barrier(2) + slow critical section, mirrors ra10) fires TWO DIFFERENT symbols on ONE account under HERMES_QUANT_PORTFOLIO_CAPS=1 and asserts combined gross EXCEEDS the cap (cross-symbol bypass; the per-symbol ra10 tick-lock does NOT serialize different symbols sharing the gross cap). The ACCOUNT-LEVEL lock fix is DEFERRED to its own flag-gated parity-tested increment (it serializes all symbols on an account and touches the live fire path — must not land unproven inline). Gap now documented by the RED proof. Keep OPEN (fix deferred). || RECONCILE 2026-06-14: STATUS: RED proof MERGED (the cross-symbol gross-cap bypass is pinned by tests/unit/test_portfolio_cap_cross_symbol_race.py, committed). The account-level-lock FIX is intentionally DEFERRED to its own flag-gated increment (it serializes all symbols on an account, touches the live fire path — must not land unproven). Stays OPEN as a fix-deferred item, NOT un-triaged. Reachable only when HERMES_QUANT_PORTFOLIO_CAPS=1.

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit b3529bc). Flag-gated default-OFF HERMES_QUANT_ACCOUNT_LOCK: a per-account fail-open lock (reusing tick_lock) wraps the cross-symbol cap-read through the state.db write, nested outside the symbol lock — closing the cross-PROCESS TOCTOU where two symbols both passed the gross cap and overshot the rail (ADR-0091 non-atomicity). Flag absent byte-identical; _portfolio_cap_clip signature unchanged (deterministic_equity reuse safe). cs60 filed (cap-clip pos_map key narrowing).

title: Reject zero/negative decision_price fills in PaperReactor instead of degrading to a fill_price=0 passthrough
description:
When _extract_decision_price returns the 0.0 sentinel (no price available), apply_slippage raises ValueError and PaperReactor catches it and proceeds at fill_price=decision_price=0.0 — a nonsensical execution record that silently corrupts the P&L ledger via zero-division in horizon-return math. The 'degrade rather than fail the fill' comment masks that a 0-price fill is not a recoverable degradation; it should be rejected. The slippage-function rejection is tested in isolation but the reactor's error-handling branch is untested. || EVIDENCE: hermes_quant/react/paper.py:244-254 — except ValueError: logger.warning(...); fill_price = decision_price; slippage_breakdown={'error':...} — degrades, does NOT raise or reject ; hermes_quant/react/slippage_model.py:182-183 — apply_slippage raises ValueError when decision_price is non-finite or <= 0 ; tests/unit/test_slippage_model.py:182 — decision_price=0.0 test covers the apply_slippage rejection directly; no test asserts PaperReactor's caller-level degrade behavior on a 0-price fill || RED PROOF LANDED 2026-06-13 (workflow wt13usy0p): tests/unit/test_paper_zero_decision_price.py pins the corrupt appended fill_price=0.0 record for BOTH the v0.1 passthrough branch and the v0.2 ValueError-degrade branch (both fall through to the unconditional ExecutionRecord + append_locked write on the LIVE bus). The degrade->reject change is DEFERRED to its own flag-gated increment (a new refusal/silence path changes live reactor behavior; gate it default-OFF, live byte-identical when OFF). Gap now documented by the test. Keep OPEN (fix deferred). || RECONCILE 2026-06-14: STATUS: RED proof MERGED (the corrupt fill_price=0.0 record is pinned for both branches). The degrade->reject FIX is DEFERRED to its own flag-gated increment (a new refusal/silence path changes live reactor behavior). Stays OPEN as fix-deferred.

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit b3529bc). Default-ON: a 0.0-sentinel decision_price (was booked free on the bus -> state.db free 0-cost position + silently dropped from settlement P&L) is now rejected to an abstain/silence record (zero_decision_price, not appended), aligning the producer with pdr_core.contracts.Fill (rejects fill_price<=0). Priced fill byte-identical.

title: Add no-lookahead CI gate coverage for FundamentalsAnalyst, OvernightDriftAnalyst, and DeliberativeCommitteeAggregator

title: Fix short-position realized-PnL sign inversion in portfolio_loader.reconstruct_portfolio (full-close formula)
description: Production settlement math records every realized short trade with the opposite sign. Today the blast radius is reported realized_pnl_total (cash/equity_total computed separately, so circuit breakers are not corrupted by THIS bug), but it is a latent landmine the instant realized-PnL is wired into cooldown/learning/reporting. Fix: drop the spurious factor -> `realized = (fill - avg_old) * old_qty`. || EVIDENCE: VERIFIED hermes_quant/daemon/portfolio_loader.py:136 — `realized = (fill - avg_old) * (-signed_qty) * (1 if old_qty > 0 else -1)`. At a full close `-signed_qty == old_qty`, so the first two factors already equal correct proceeds-vs-basis; the trailing `* (1 if old_qty>0 else -1)` term inverts shorts only. ; Numeric proof from candidate: long-win=+10 (correct), long-loss=-10 (correct), short-win returns -10 (should be +10), short-loss returns +10 (should be -10). ; Shorts are first-class (protocol.py:49 `-1=short`; portfolio_loader.py:99 `signed_qty = qty if side=='buy' else -qty`); the NotImplementedError guard at lines 120-131 blocks only partial closes / direction flips, so a clean short-open -> short-full-close reaches line 136. ; Live-wired: daemon/main.py:183 portfolio_for -> reconstruct_portfolio each tick; value flows to Portfolio.realized_pnl_total (protocol.py:294). No test exercises the short-close realized sign (tests/unit/test_portfolio_state.py targets portfolio/state.py::reconstruct_portfolio_state, a different function). ; Distinct from ra01 (dual-ledger cumulative-delta vs latest-target semantics) and from cr00 (unit basis) — this is a sign-convention error in the daemon settlement reconstructor, not a ledger-semantics or unit issue. || VERIFIED 2026-06-13: portfolio_loader.py:136 short-sign inversion confirmed in code, BUT reconstruct_portfolio is called ONLY by daemon/main.py:183, and the daemon is vestigial (ra04 — no live cron runs run_one_tick/daemon.main). Real bug in dead code. Routed to Increment 4 (delete vestigial daemon cluster) which removes the whole class. Relabel: not live. || RESOLVED-BY-DELETION f998369: the short-PnL sign inversion lived in daemon/portfolio_loader's reconstruct_portfolio called ONLY by the deleted daemon.main. NOTE: portfolio_loader.py itself is KEPT (2 importers) — re-verify the surviving callers don't hit the buggy full-close branch; if any live caller does, re-open as a live bug. (Likely moot: daemon.main was the only full-close driver.) || FIX LANDED 2026-06-13 (workflow wt13usy0p, orchestrator-verified): portfolio_loader.py:153 drops the spurious *(1 if old_qty>0 else -1); long path byte-identical (test_buy_then_close==2000.0 GREEN), short sign corrected (+ new test_short_then_cover_realizes_positive_pnl==+100). Consumer re-confirmed report-only (pdr_core_adapter omits realized_pnl_total from the gate projection; quant-playbook-weekly reads pf.positions only). CAVEAT: cs14 proves the loader's schema_version==1 filter drops every LIVE record, so this fix is correct-but-currently-UNREACHABLE in prod until cs14 lands. Keep OPEN pending cs14 + a prod-path test. || CLOSED 2026-06-14 (bookkeeping reconcile): fix landed+merged (commit 88dc1e0): short-PnL sign corrected, long byte-identical, report-only consumer. Reachability gated by cs14 (also merged). RESOLVED.

title: Thread durable peak_equity and session-anchored daily_open_equity through reconstruct_portfolio (drawdown + daily-loss breakers fail open)
description:
The deterministic gate is the FINAL money-safety authority, and its Rule-1/Rule-2 circuit breakers read drawdown/daily-loss against an inception baseline that drifts away from reality every session. Net effect is fail-OPEN: a profitable-from-inception account can suffer a large intraday or peak-to-trough drawdown without tripping either breaker. Fix: persist a durable peak_equity and a session-anchored daily_open_equity across reconstructions rather than hardcoding initial_cash. || EVIDENCE: VERIFIED hermes_quant/daemon/portfolio_loader.py:85 `daily_open_equity = initial_cash` — never reset to start-of-session equity; Portfolio.daily_loss_pct (protocol.py:313-320) then measures loss-since-inception. While cumulative equity stays above initial_cash, daily_loss_pct clamps to 0 via max(0.0,...) after an intraday drop, so Rule-2 daily_loss_circuit_breaker (default 5%) never trips — fail-open. ; VERIFIED hermes_quant/daemon/portfolio_loader.py:86 `peak_equity = initial_cash` and :167 `peak_equity = max(peak_equity, equity_total)` runs ONCE after the loop, so the returned peak is just max(initial_cash, final_equity); the true rolling peak is lost. An account that hit 130k then fell to 115k reads peak=115k -> drawdown 0 instead of ~11.5%, so Rule-1 drawdown_circuit_breaker (default 15%) can fail to trip. ; Stateless live wiring: daemon/main.py:182-188 calls reconstruct_portfolio fresh each tick passing only initial_cash; no durable peak or session-open equity is threaded in, so both baselines reset to inception every tick. ; Prior review docs/reviews/2026-06-07-quant-deep-review/facet-riskgate.txt:13 audited only the gate's NaN-handling of drawdown_pct/daily_loss_pct, not the upstream baselines — unfiled in cr00-cr19/ra00-ra11. || VERIFIED 2026-06-13: peak_equity/daily_open_equity=initial_cash baselines confirmed, BUT same vestigial daemon/main.py path (ra04). Real fail-open in dead code. The LIVE breaker baseline is the autonomous/cap path, not this reconstructor. Routed to Increment 4. Relabel: not live. || DEFERRED 2026-06-13 (workflow wt13usy0p, orchestrator-verified): the fail-OPEN formula is real (portfolio_loader daily_open_equity/peak_equity hardcoded to initial_cash => Rule-1/Rule-2 measure drawdown since INCEPTION) BUT the loader's Portfolio is NOT wired to the live FINAL-authority gate today: the live autonomous tick feeds risk/gate.py a SYNTHETIC flat portfolio (advisor.py:128-148, 'does NOT read real broker state'); the loader's only live consumer (quant-playbook-weekly) never calls risk/gate.py; settlement_loop's loader-join is a v0.1.2-future comment. Per the safety gradient (when unsure, downgrade): landing a session-anchored daily_open_equity/durable-peak fix detached changes a number NO live gate reads — route it AS PART OF the future gate-wiring increment under its own parity test. (Also gated behind cs14: the loader reads a dead schema today.) || RECONCILE 2026-06-14: STATUS: real fail-OPEN formula, but the loader's Portfolio is NOT wired to the live FINAL-authority gate (the live tick uses a synthetic flat portfolio). DEFERRED to the future gate-wiring increment under its own parity test (landing it detached changes a number no live gate reads). Stays OPEN, gate-wiring-blocked.

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-15 (commit on branch; MEGA-workflow, 6 passes). A new risk/baseline_store.py (durable monotonic peak_equity + session-anchored daily_open_equity, mirroring HaltStateSQLite: state.db row + atomic JSON mirror + WAL + RLock + fail-closed read, keyed account+asset_class) + a default-OFF gate seam (baseline_store param defaults None -> byte-identical). When injected, Rule-1 drawdown computes vs max(in-memory, durable peak) and Rule-2 daily-loss vs the durable session-open BEFORE the trip logic — the breaker can only trip EARLIER/equally, never later; fail-CLOSED on a durable-read failure. Research-grounded (Magdon-Ismail MDD / Chekhlov-Uryasev CDaR; fail-closed cardinal per Knight Capital). Gate Rules 0,3-7 + sizing ladder UNCHANGED; fresh account byte-identical. 64 tests green. The fail-OPEN drawdown/daily-loss baseline drift is CLOSED at the gate. LIVE store-injection (the producer that builds + passes the baseline_store) is a follow-up -> cs86.

title: Add a cap-silence branch to quant_approve so a portfolio-cap-silenced fill is not reported as success:True with the original size
description: Operator-facing dishonesty on the money seam: a fire the cap refused is reported as a successful approval with the original un-clipped size while zero capital moved and nothing hit the bus, and the proposal is consumed so it cannot be re-approved when headroom frees. This is the exact failure class the admissibility branch (lines 758-782, 'Wave-S review … operator-facing dishonesty') was added to prevent; the cap-silence path never got the same treatment. Fix: mirror the admissibility branch for the silence flag (keep pending, report success:False / realized 0.0). || EVIDENCE: VERIFIED hermes_quant/tools.py:764-782 — quant_approve handles only the `admissibility_rejected` flag (keeps proposal pending, returns success:False). There is NO branch for the cap-silence flag set at react/paper.py:495-496 (`reactor_metadata.silenced` / `silence_reason='portfolio_cap_...'`). ; VERIFIED hermes_quant/tools.py:806-811 — on a cap-silenced ExecutionRecord the code still calls store.approve(...), advancing the proposal to `approved` (consuming it; cannot be re-approved when headroom later frees). ; VERIFIED hermes_quant/tools.py:837-846 — returns success:True, state:approved, and `fill_size_pct: fill_size_pct` = the ORIGINAL requested size (e.g. 0.10), not the realized 0.0; the embedded execution dict has fill_size_pct=0.0 / silenced=True. ; VERIFIED react/paper.py:488-501 — the silenced record sets fill_size_pct=0.0 + reactor_metadata={silenced:True,silence_reason:...} and is NOT appended to the bus (early-return). The same path misreports the partial-scale case (cap scales 0.10->0.04 but line 843 still reports 0.10). ; Distinct from cr01 (cap-clip units) and from the de-risk-guard bypass items — this is a control-flow/reporting gap in quant_approve present even with correct cap units. || FIXED commit e1b428c (TDD, live-verified quant_approve): added cap-silence branch mirroring admissibility — pending+success:False+realized 0.0. 21/21 hitl suite.

title: Assert result.passed (not just structural fields) in the ADR-0006 shuffle-timestamps release-blocker test
description: test_shuffle_timestamps_invariant_via_evaluation_module is filed as the ADR-0006 release-blocker fence but never asserts result.passed nor that real_score differs from shuffled_mean. An analyst whose confidence_raw is identical on real vs shuffled bars emits p_value=1.0 and passes both structural assertions, so no analyst in the parametrize list is actually statistically tested for lookahead in CI. Fix: assert result.passed (and real_score > shuffled mean) at the deterministic seed/n_shuffles; the flakiness comment is invalid for the fixed seed used. || EVIDENCE: VERIFIED tests/test_no_lookahead.py:365-366 — the only assertions are `assert 0.0 <= result.p_value <= 1.0` and `assert len(result.shuffled_scores) == 8`; result.passed and real_score-vs-shuffled_mean are never asserted. ; VERIFIED tests/test_no_lookahead.py:362-364 — comment: 'We assert structural fields, not the pass/fail (which can be flaky on small n_shuffles)'. But the test calls shuffle_timestamps_test with n_shuffles=8, seed=42 (lines 352-354) — deterministic, so the flakiness rationale is misapplied. ; hermes_quant/evaluation/lookahead.py:139-140 — p_value = (n_at_or_above+1)/(n_shuffles+1) Laplace-smoothed; an analyst returning identical confidence_raw on real and shuffled inputs yields p_value=9/9=1.0 > alpha -> passed=True, so a constant/position-based analyst passes both structural asserts. ; Distinct from cr06: cr06 is about parametrize COVERAGE (and the parametrize at tests/test_no_lookahead.py:304-311 now already includes ClassicalTAAnalyst, MicrostructureLite, FundamentalsAnalyst, OvernightDriftAnalyst). This item is that the test which IS wired never makes a lookahead assertion. || FIXED commit ada3aa7: no-lookahead shuffle gate de-vacuumed (asserts result.passed + real_score vs shuffled-mean). 31 pass.

title: Forward as_of through fetch_with_chain so the live daemon tick path enforces the leaf-level lookahead filter
description: ADR-0005 Wave C.1 pushed as_of enforcement down to individual providers, but fetch_with_chain — the multi-provider fallback engine used by the live tick daemon — has no as_of parameter and never passes one, so every provider call routed through the chain skips the leaf-level filter. In the daemon tick path the computed asof boundary is never forwarded, so the tick loop can receive bars up to wall-clock now rather than up to the decision asof. Fix: add an as_of kwarg to fetch_with_chain, forward it to each provider.fetch_bars, and thread the tick's asof at tick_loop.py:262. || EVIDENCE: VERIFIED hermes_quant/data/base.py:104-113 — fetch_with_chain signature has no as_of parameter; :143 `bars = provider.fetch_bars(asset, timeframe, start, end, use_cache=use_cache)` passes no as_of. ; hermes_quant/daemon/tick_loop.py:262-268 — the live daemon calls fetch_with_chain(...) with no as_of; the asof boundary computed earlier in the tick is never forwarded to the data layer. ; yfinance/alphavantage/ccxt providers apply the ADR-0005 Wave C.1 as_of filter only when `as_of is not None`; routed through fetch_with_chain the filter is disabled and the full [start,end] window up to wall-clock now is returned. ; tests/test_no_lookahead.py:174-204 (test_advisor_passes_as_of_to_provider) covers only the recommend() path through the advisor, not the fetch_with_chain path the daemon uses. || VERIFIED-REAL-BUT-LATENT: fetch_with_chain lacks as_of, BUT it is called ONLY by daemon/tick_loop.py (vestigial daemon, ra04). The LIVE advisor path does NOT use fetch_with_chain (uses get_resampled_history, fixed in cs05). Routed to Increment 4 (delete vestigial daemon). Not live; demoted P1->P2. || RESOLVED-BY-DELETION f998369: fetch_with_chain-no-as_of mattered only on the deleted daemon tick_loop path; the live advisor path uses get_resampled_history (fixed in cs05).

title: Clip resampled horizon bars to timestamp <= asof_ts on the horizon_cache hit path (partial-period buckets leak future daily bars)
description: On a daily-parquet cache hit (keyed by UTC calendar date), bars are returned and resampled with no timestamp filter, and resample aggregates partial-period buckets — e.g. a 1w resample at Wednesday noon emits a W-FRI bar that includes Thursday/Friday daily bars from the cached file. The result is a completed-looking weekly/monthly/quarterly bar that actually includes future daily bars. Fix is structural: clip the resampled output to `timestamp <= asof_ts` (and ideally drop still-forming buckets) on both paths. || EVIDENCE: VERIFIED hermes_quant/data/horizon_cache.py:216 `daily = _load_from_cache(symbol, asof_date_str)` — cache key is a calendar-date string; on a hit no as_of filter is applied to the returned DataFrame (_load_from_cache returns raw parquet, no timestamp predicate). ; VERIFIED hermes_quant/data/horizon_cache.py:273-276 `return resample_to_horizon(daily, timeframe)` — called on the unfiltered daily frame for BOTH cache-hit and post-fetch paths, with no post-resample asof cutoff. ; VERIFIED the cold path at horizon_cache.py:239 correctly passes `as_of=asof_ts` to the provider — only the cache-hit path skips the cutoff. ; resample_to_horizon uses pandas.resample(rule).agg(...) where dropna removes only empty buckets, not future-dated ones — a partial W-FRI/BME bucket whose period-end label is after asof_ts is emitted as a completed-looking weekly/monthly bar containing 2-3 future daily bars. ; advisor.py _fetch_bars_for_horizon delegates 1w/1M/1Q to get_resampled_history with asof=asof_ts and trusts the cache to honor the cutoff, which it does not on a hit. || FIXED commit e1b428c (TDD, live-verified via advisor.py:454): clip daily to asof before resample + drop still-forming buckets. RED showed ~7wk future leak. 222 passed in slice.

title: Extend the options_gate NaN guard (or O6 site) to total_bpr / options_buying_power / premium_received (NaN total_bpr ADMITS at O6)
description: Direct residual of this session's cr02 fix: cr02 added a non-finite guard for spot and nav only, but the O6 BPR-buffer comparison consumes total_bpr (an external portfolio aggregate) and premium_received (from external chain mid quotes via `float(short.mid or 0.0)`), neither finite-checked. A NaN in either makes O6 always-False and the gate ADMITS — the canonical NaN-fail-open class. P2 not P1 because the options gate is default-OFF (HERMES_QUANT_OPTIONS_GATE), so no current live exposure, but cr02 itself was filed/fixed under that identical default-OFF condition. Fix: extend the options_gate.py:507 isfinite check to total_bpr/options_buying_power/premium_received (or guard at the O6 site) and harden recipes.py:225 against a NaN mid. || EVIDENCE: VERIFIED hermes_quant/risk/options_gate.py:507 — the cr02 guard checks only `math.isfinite(spot)` and `math.isfinite(nav)`; it does NOT cover total_bpr or premium_received. ; VERIFIED hermes_quant/risk/options_gate.py:664 — O6 `if total_bpr + bpr > cfg.bpr_buffer_pct_nav * nav:` — `NaN > x` is always False, so a NaN total_bpr passes the buffer check (fail-open), while inf correctly silences via bpr_buffer. ; hermes_quant/options/recipes.py:174 `total_bpr: float = 0.0` is caller-supplied and never finite-validated on the recipe->gate path; options_buying_power (line 173) likewise unguarded. ; hermes_quant/options/recipes.py:225 `premium_received = float(short.mid or 0.0) * 100.0` — `or 0.0` guards None but NOT a NaN mid quote, so NaN mid -> NaN premium_received -> _bpr() -> O6 fail-open. ; cr02 (.seeds/issues.jsonl) is explicitly 'Guard NaN spot/nav/greeks'; its FIXED note (commit 6e17488) covers isfinite spot/nav + non-finite greeks. The BPR/premium input class is out of cr02's stated scope; no existing seed covers total_bpr/bpr_buffer/premium_received. || FIXED commit 5add243: non-finite guard extended to total_bpr/options_buying_power/premium_received + recipes _finite_mid. Reviewer reproduced the O6 fail-open. 44/44 + 79/79.

title: Make settlement fee-drag dimensionally consistent in join_exit_fills / compute_horizon_return (NAV-fraction qty divided into dollar fees)
description: Additive, not-yet-wired measurement infrastructure with paper fees = 0, so no live corruption today. But the moment a live broker populates reactor_metadata.fees in dollars (or a seed wires join_exit_fills as the calibrator/reflector input the docstring promises), realized_return is mis-netted by a factor of NAV — a sizing-relevant error since calibrated alpha drives Kelly. Fix: make qty and fees share units (dollar notional throughout, or convert fees to a NAV fraction before dividing by an NAV-fraction notional). || EVIDENCE: hermes_quant/daemon/settlement_loop.py:748-751 — `entry_notional = entry_price * matched; fee_drag = prorated_fees / entry_notional`, but _normalize_exec_record (lines 535-540) sets `qty = abs(fill_size_pct)` (a NAV fraction, e.g. 0.10) while fees come from explicit `fees` / `reactor_metadata.fees` in quote currency (dollars). So fee_drag = dollars / (price * nav_fraction) is off by a factor of NAV; the gross price-ratio term is scale-free but the fee leg is not, contradicting the docstring's 'scale-free' claim. ; compute_horizon_return (lines 883-887) repeats the same `entry_notional = ep * q` denominator and is exposed to callers/tests with the same trap. ; react/paper.py::_record_to_dict (lines 35-55) serializes fill_size_pct (NAV fraction) + reactor_metadata, with no top-level dollar qty and no top-level fees; for paper, fees default to 0.0 so the bug is LATENT today. ; settlement_loop.py:379-381 states there is NO production caller yet (daemon/main.py wires construct_realized_outcomes + dispatch_settlement, not join_exit_fills). ; Distinct from ra01 (dual-ledger reconstructor semantics) — this is a units error inside the not-yet-wired settlement return math. || RESOLVED-BY-DELETION f998369: settlement fee-drag dimensional issue was in join_exit_fills which had NO production caller (dead daemon path). settlement_loop.py KEPT but join_exit_fills remains uncalled; folded into i0c scope if ever wired.

title: Subsample non-overlapping windows (or gate on effective N) in bootstrap_calibrator isotonic fit (autocorrelated samples inflate the N>=200 gate)
description: Overlapping-window double-counting in the only learning calibrator. It does not corrupt cash directly but it inflates the apparent sample size and fits a calibration curve on pseudo-replicated outcomes, biasing the calibrated P(correct) that sizes every trade. Fix: subsample non-overlapping windows (stride = horizon_bars) for the fit, or down-weight by an effective-sample-size correction, and gate on effective N rather than raw count. || EVIDENCE: hermes_quant/training/bootstrap_calibrator.py:189 `for t in range(min_context_bars, n - horizon_bars):` steps t by 1, and :206 settles each sample against a horizon_bars-wide forward window (default horizon_bars=4). Consecutive samples at t and t+1 share 3 of 4 forward bars, so direction_correct outcomes are heavily autocorrelated, not i.i.d. ; IsotonicCalibrator.n_min_samples = 200 (calibrators.py:146) gates the fit on raw COUNT (bootstrap_calibrator.py:374 `if n_samples < min_samples`) with no overlap / effective-sample correction — ~50 independent 4-bar holds satisfy the 200 gate. ; The fitted IsotonicCalibrator is the production calibrator converting raw confidence to the calibrated probability the risk gate feeds into expected_signed_edge and quarter_kelly_size (risk/gate.py:618-622, 683-690), so a biased curve flows straight into position sizing. ; No existing seed covers calibrator overlapping-window double-counting. || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 840851f). SCOPE-CORRECTED: the workflow's Prove caught an orchestrator file-pointer error (scoped validation.py, which has no horizon/overlap bug) and fixed the REAL bug at training/bootstrap_calibrator.py:189 (the canonical seed's named location): strided the calibration walk by horizon_bars so samples are i.i.d. non-overlapping blocks -> len(all_raw) counts only non-overlapping outcomes -> the min_samples=200 gate + IsotonicCalibrator.n_min_samples=200 fit-guard become EFFECTIVE-N gates -> de-biases the calibration curve that sizes every trade (BMAAggregator->signal.confidence->risk/gate quarter_kelly). Stride-subsample chosen over ESS (fixes both the gate count AND the isotonic fit). horizon=1 byte-identical; production defaults unchanged; correctness-positive + conservative (no live mid-run shrink — pickle only changes on explicit re-bootstrap). 14 tests green (RED-revert confirmed). OPERATOR: re-bootstrap on a ~4x larger universe/lookback so the calibrator clears the honest 200 floor at H=4 (else ColdStartCalibrator fallback, silence-by-default safe). NEW critique cs39 (validation.py excess date-misalignment).

title: Observe the reactor return value in the autonomous tick so a reactor-seam cap silence is not counted as a fire with phantom headroom
description: The autonomous fire loop's running headroom model, fire count, and reported execution_id all assume reactor.execute always fills at effective_size. Because the seam clip reads a different ledger (state.db incl. det-equity true-share fills) than the autonomous clip (bus, paper-only), a reactor-seam silence is both undetected and counted as a fire, with phantom headroom consumed for the rest of the tick — corrupting the cap math for every subsequent pick. Fix: have _react return the ExecutionRecord and have the caller skip the fire count / position accrual when reactor_metadata.silenced is set. || EVIDENCE: hermes_quant/autonomous.py:905,928 — _react() calls reactor.execute(...) but discards the returned ExecutionRecord and unconditionally returns `pid`; it cannot observe whether the reactor's own _portfolio_cap_clip silenced the fill. ; hermes_quant/autonomous.py:801-816 — on return it does fires_this_tick += 1, sets decision.execution_id = pid, and records portfolio_state.positions[entry.symbol] = effective_size even if the reactor wrote nothing to the bus. ; Two ledgers diverge: autonomous builds portfolio_state via reconstruct_portfolio_state() (portfolio/state.py:35-121) reading executions.jsonl with reactor_filter='paper' (line 40, EXCLUDES deterministic-equity / alpaca_paper / multileg), while the reactor-seam clip reads ps.get_positions('paper-default') from state.db (react/paper.py:438-445) which INCLUDES det-equity fills. ; HERMES_QUANT_DETERMINISTIC_EQUITY=1 and HERMES_QUANT_PORTFOLIO_CAPS=1 are both armed live (docs/FLAGS.md:50-51), so the bus-reconstruct (autonomous) sees a SMALLER book than state.db (reactor seam); the seam can silence a fire the autonomous-level clip passed. ; Distinct from ra02 (autonomous hardcodes PaperReactor / raw-Alpaca POST bypassing the seam) — this is the discard-of-return-value + phantom-headroom + deterministic ledger divergence, and distinct from the premortem §3.2 concurrency race (over-shrinking size). || RESOLVED-BY-DELETION f998369: the autonomous-tick reactor-return / dead-daemon ledger divergence concern; the daemon half is gone. The autonomous.py live half (if any residual) is ra02/Inc-2 shadow territory.

The moment any reactor carries a non-default account on the record (the forward-compat path the bus-append already supports at react/paper.py:316-318), the cap would read paper-default's book while the fill lands in another partition — a cap-checked-but-not-enforced gap. No live behavior change. title: Restrict the AlphaVantage range or always apply the as_of filter (start/end are ignored; ~100-bar window leaks past the asof anchor on the chain path)
description: AlphaVantage TIME_SERIES_DAILY always returns the last ~100 daily bars and silently ignores start/end (documented behavior). The sole lookahead protection is the as_of post-filter, applied only when as_of is not None; invoked via fetch_with_chain (no as_of) it returns bars up to wall-clock today regardless of the backtest anchor — an unprotected leak path for any chain caller. P2 because it is gated behind the fetch_with_chain as_of fix, but worth an independent provider-level guard. Fix: prune to `timestamp <= end` even when as_of is absent (treat end as the implicit cutoff). || EVIDENCE: VERIFIED hermes_quant/data/alphavantage_provider.py:258-263 docstring — 'AV compact returns the last ~100 daily bars regardless; we filter to timestamp <= as_of only (no lower-bound prune ...)'. ; VERIFIED hermes_quant/data/alphavantage_provider.py:286-293 — the params dict is built from function/symbol/outputsize/datatype/apikey only; start and end are never forwarded to the HTTP request. ; alphavantage_provider.py:368-375 — only the as_of post-filter is applied; when as_of=None (e.g. via fetch_with_chain which passes no as_of) the full ~100-bar window up to today is returned regardless of the requested end. ; data/base.py:143 — fetch_with_chain calls provider.fetch_bars without as_of, disabling AV's only lookahead guard on the chain path. Distinct from the fetch_with_chain item: that one is the chain not forwarding as_of; this is AV having no range-restriction fallback even when called directly without as_of. || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit f57e13f). AlphaVantage fetch_bars now prunes to the TIGHTEST of as_of/end (cutoff=min over whichever present; both-None=no prune, the only up-to-now opt-in — end verified never None on live chain paths). Closes the fetch_with_chain (no-as_of) lookahead leak where AV returned ~100 bars to wall-clock today past the backtest `end` anchor; as_of behavior preserved (min monotone). Mirrors yfinance's as_of prune. 25 AV tests green (7 leak/cutoff/as_of); alphavantage_provider.py only. Latent-but-real (chain default-OFF behind HERMES_QUANT_DATA_FALLBACK, AV appended last). NEW critique cs38 (cache-hit lookahead, distinct module).

title: Default-ON (or asof-derive) the FundamentalsProvider reporting-lag filter — as_of_date alone leaks ~45 days of fundamental lookahead in backtests
description: The B34 reporting-lag filter was built precisely to prevent fundamental lookahead — a Q4 filing with period_end Dec-31 is not knowable until ~45 days later. With the flag OFF (the default), read_latest only requires as_of_date (the cron-fetch day) <= as_of, not that the filing was actually public by then, leaking up to 45+ days of fundamental data too early in every backtest. The flag's own docstring says it 'only ever TIGHTENS what is visible', so making it default-ON (or deriving the cutoff from period_end+lag whenever an as_of is supplied) is safe. Fix: default-ON the lag filter, or apply period_end+lag in read_latest whenever as_of is provided. || EVIDENCE: hermes_quant/data/fundamentals_provider.py:63-80 — 'When HERMES_QUANT_FUNDAMENTALS_REPORTING_LAG is truthy (default OFF)' the reporting-lag filter that prevents fundamental lookahead is disabled by default; _reporting_lag_flag_on() (110-123) returns False unless the env var is set. ; fundamentals_provider.py:303-343 — _apply_reporting_lag_filter() is a no-op when the flag is OFF (returns df unchanged). ; fundamentals_provider.py:379-389 — read_latest with as_of filters only on as_of_date <= as_of (the day the datum was cached), not on period_end+lag (when it became knowable). period_end is stored (line 661, from mostRecentQuarter) but a Q4 with period_end=Dec-31 may not file until mid-Feb (45d+ later). ; analysts/fundamentals.py:186-225 — FundamentalsAnalyst._fetch_fundamentals calls provider.read_latest(ticker, as_of=asof); with the flag OFF a backtest at Jan-15 that cached on Jan-14 sees Q4 data with period_end=Dec-31 that was not public until ~Feb-14. ; No existing seed covers the reporting-lag default-OFF lookahead hole; distinct from cr06 (no-lookahead CI coverage). || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit e0ae4cd). Flipped the B34 HERMES_QUANT_FUNDAMENTALS_REPORTING_LAG flag to default-ON (was default-OFF), so read_latest applies the reporting-lag-adjusted as_of predicate (effective_knowable=(report_date or period_end or as_of_date)+45d <= as_of) by default — closing the ~30-45d fundamental-lookahead leak (a Q4 period_end=Dec-31 datum cached mid-Jan was returned to a Jan-15 decision ~30d before knowable Feb-14). SAFETY-CLASS flag-gate: the only as_of= caller is the LIVE FundamentalsAnalyst (ADR-0004 gate input), so default-ON makes it strictly MORE conservative (drops not-yet-public data, silence-by-default) and an explicit OFF (=0/false/no/off/empty) reverts to the BYTE-IDENTICAL pre-B34 path (instant operator kill switch — empirically verified unset->ON, 0->OFF). lag=45d from DEFAULT_REPORTING_LAG_DAYS (code constant, not invented). 8 consumer regressions fixed by stamping a PUBLIC period_end in fixtures (proving the active filter admits an already-public quarter), NOT by pinning the flag; 41 passed+1 skipped flag-unpinned. OPERATOR NOTE in docstring: against an old-schema/stale cache the default-ON filter goes FULL-DARK (as_of_date+45d fallback) until the prewarm cron writes real period_end/report_date rows + the 45d lag elapses — gate the live-enablement flip on cache schema/freshness. NEW critique cs40/cs41/cs42.

title: pdr_core Fill stamps schema_version=int 1, but is_absolute_target_record() only accepts None or the STRING 'absolute-target-v1' — a Fill-driven record reads as true-delta and re-inflates (re-opens the AAPL-12x/BA-6x defect)
description: VERIFIED in isolation against the real code: contracts.py:193 FILL_SCHEMA_VERSION:int=1; react/base.py:27-28 is_absolute_target_record returns `v is None or v == 'absolute-target-v1'`. Confirmed: is_absolute_target_record({'schema_version':1}) -> False, ({'schema_version':'absolute-target-v1'}) -> True, ({}) -> True. So a serialized pdr_core Fill (default int 1) classifies as a TRUE-DELTA record; fill_delta_normalizer.delta_from_net then passes the absolute target through as a raw per-fill delta, so N re-affirmations of 0.05 fold to N*0.05 — the exact inflation Option E exists to prevent, in the very contract built to fix it. Type mismatch between the contract's version sentinel and the only classifier function. Fix: emit the string sentinel OR widen is_absolute_target_record to accept the int. NEW: not in any tracked id; orthogonal to i0a/i0b/i0c (those wired the existing string-sentinel ExecutionRecord, this is the new pdr_core Fill contract crossing the same seam). || FIXED 2026-06-13 (contract-layer commit).

title: pdr_core purity gate omits governance/evidence/state from FORBIDDEN_HERMES_SUBMODULES (and pydantic from FORBIDDEN_TOP_LEVEL) — the gate/BMA/kelly port can import governance.invariants/state and stay green
description: VERIFIED against tests/pdr_core/test_contract_purity.py:36-65: FORBIDDEN_HERMES_SUBMODULES lists daemon/react/advisor/tools/tool_schemas/data/agents/consumers/observability/reconcile/reporting/cli/discord_slash/committee_runner but NOT governance, evidence, or state; FORBIDDEN_TOP_LEVEL lists broker/heavy-IO packages but NOT pydantic (nor pandas/numpy). Both Gate-1a (subprocess sys.modules, lines 98-130) and Gate-1b (static AST walk, lines 156-171) iterate the same incomplete list. contracts.py:60-64 documents the core keeps its OWN POSITION_LADDER copy precisely because the purity contract forbids reaching into governance — yet the enforcing gate does not list governance. This is the enabling risk for the entire port: a ported gate lazily importing governance.audit_log (which pulls pydantic, the explicitly-forbidden agents-shell dep) would PASS today. RECOMMENDATION: tighten the FORBIDDEN lists (add governance, evidence, state, pydantic; consider protocol/calibrators/learning) BEFORE step 1, so the gate guards the boundary it claims. NEW: latent hole, becomes an active leak the moment the port lands. || FIXED 2026-06-13 (contract-layer commit).

title: pdr_core Fill has NO __post_init__ — NaN/negative fill_price and NaN fill_size_pct are accepted, and a NaN fill_size_pct poisons FillDeltaNormalizer running_net for the entire (account,asset_class,asset) bucket
description: VERIFIED: AnalystView (contracts.py:134) and Proposal (contracts.py:180) define __post_init__ validation; Fill (contracts.py:197-219) defines NONE. Confirmed Fill(fill_price=nan, fill_size_pct=nan) and Fill(fill_price=-5.0) both construct without error. fill_delta_normalizer.py:140-142 does net_map[key]=absolute; a NaN absolute makes running_net NaN, and every later delta = target - NaN = NaN, silently corrupting all subsequent folds for that bucket and breaking the 'hard architectural gate' no-two-views guarantee (normalizer docstring lines 21-25). fill_price<=0 should also be rejected: a $0/negative premium zeroes/sign-flips the cash basis (portfolio_state.py contract-multiplier path). The two TRIAD siblings reject non-finite/out-of-range at construction; Fill — the reaction feedback the carry-forward gate trusts — is unguarded. NEW. || FIXED 2026-06-13 (contract-layer commit).

title: Flag-transition hazard: enabling HERMES_QUANT_DELTA_NORMALIZER without a forced full rebuild differences new absolute targets against an inflated flag-OFF-built state.db, emitting phantom sells/flips
description: VERIFIED against portfolio_state.py: line 370 (rebuild) and line 640 (incremental) read os.environ HERMES_QUANT_DELTA_NORMALIZER independently at call time; line 643 pos_delta = delta_from_net(record, old_qty) seeds net from the PERSISTED positions row (line 617-624). There is NO regime marker in state.db and NO forced rebuild on flag transition. verdict.md:38 directive #6 states flag-OFF is bit-for-bit current (still INFLATED) behavior, and the heal only happens 'on the next full rebuild with the flag on' — but nothing couples the flag flip to a rebuild. Worked example: old_qty=0.15 (3x inflated flag-OFF reaffirmations of 0.05) + incoming reaffirm target 0.05 => delta_from_net = 0.05-0.15 = -0.10, a spurious 10% sell on a no-op. The verdict's P0-hunt analyzed incremental-vs-rebuild divergence WITHIN one regime (attack 2) but NEVER the cross-regime transition. NEW and distinct from i0a/verdict attack-2; this is the foot-gun on the exact default-OFF eval-gated rollout path the work is meant to make safe. Needs a state.db regime-stamp that forces a rebuild on mismatch, or a hard refusal of the incremental path until a flag-ON rebuild has run. || FIX LANDED 2026-06-13 (workflow wt13usy0p, orchestrator-verified): added a state.db PRAGMA user_version regime-stamp (portfolio_state.py): reconstruct_from stamps the regime that BUILT the db (0=OFF/legacy, 1=ON) inside its BEGIN IMMEDIATE; apply_execution calls _check_regime_stamp() BEFORE the fold and HARD-REFUSES (RuntimeError, raised outside the swallowing try/except) when a POPULATED db's stamp != the current flag regime — refuse+surface, never phantom-sell. Byte-identity rail: user_version=0 doubles as never-stamped AND flag-OFF, and the default regime is 0, so the default path NEVER fires the guard (empirically verified: flag-OFF apply on a fresh db leaves user_version 0 and succeeds). 3 regime tests pass; 167 state+paper+tick-lock regression pass. RESOLVED. || CLOSED 2026-06-14 (bookkeeping reconcile): fix landed+merged (commit 88dc1e0): state.db PRAGMA user_version regime-stamp hard-refuses a flag-flip mismatch (fail-loud, never phantom-sell); flag-OFF byte-identical. RESOLVED.

title: asset_class string divergence: pdr_core/protocol use 'option' but the money-state 100x contract-multiplier keys off 'us_option' — a host-blind core settling option fills off the contract asset_class would miss the multiplier (100x undervaluation)
description: VERIFIED: pdr_core/contracts.py:47 AssetClass = Literal['crypto','equity','etf','fx','option'] (protocol.py:65 identical); react/multileg.py:569 stamps asset_class='us_option' on actual option fills; portfolio_state.py:446,560,714,1072 gate _CONTRACT_MULTIPLIER=100.0 ONLY when asset_class=='us_option'. Grep confirms 'us_option' appears only in multileg.py + portfolio_state.py; the contract Literal has no 'us_option' member, so the string 'option' never triggers the multiplier. The pdr_core contract is positioned as the host-blind seam that will own sizing+settlement; if future core settlement applies the multiplier off Fill/AnalystView.asset_class (only ever 'option' per the Literal), an option fill is undervalued 100x — the same class of bug ADR-0088 F1 fixed once in the host. There is no shared canonical string. Either the core learns 'us_option' or the host normalizes before crossing the seam. NEW — surfaces when the BMA/gate port (steps 4/6) starts consuming asset_class for money arithmetic. || ANALYSIS 2026-06-13 (verified): AssetClass Literal lists 'option' in BOTH pdr_core/contracts.py:47 AND protocol.py:65, but the 100x _CONTRACT_MULTIPLIER is keyed on the runtime string 'us_option' (multileg.py:569 stamps it; portfolio_state.py:446/560/714/1073 gate on it). RESOLUTION PATH (deferred to the shell-adoption increment, with justification): the fix is ONE canonical string + a shell adapter normalizing option<->us_option at the seam — NOT widening the Literal (would let two spellings coexist, worsening the fork) and NOT renaming us_option in live money code mid-port (behavior-touching, needs parity scaffolding the shell increment provides). Latent until the core aggregate/settlement consumes asset_class for option arithmetic. Pinned here so it is not lost. || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 1b9a338). Option A (additive): widened BOTH AssetClass Literals (pdr_core/contracts.py + protocol.py, kept byte-equal) to include "us_option" (type-hint-only — every asset_class field is `str`, no exhaustive-match/validator to break) + added OPTION_ASSET_CLASSES=frozenset({option,us_option}) + is_option_asset_class() to pdr_core/contracts.py (stdlib-only, passes the purity gate) so future ADR-0092 settlement keys on the option FAMILY not a single string. LIVE MONEY-STATE BYTE-UNCHANGED: portfolio_state.py + multileg.py 0-diff — the 6 ×100 gate sites still compare == "us_option", _CONTRACT_MULTIPLIER stays 100.0. Closes the latent silent-100×-option-undervaluation trap (a future-core keying ×100 on bare =="option" would settle a us_option Fill at 1.0). Drift-guard test pins the two Literals equal + the recognizer family. 418 tests green. NEW critique cs44 (multi_leg parent double-books cash — P2 money-state) + cs45 (fundamentals mis-classifies us_option as equity — same token divergence in the analyst).

title: FillDeltaNormalizer mixed-schema seeding asymmetry: a true-delta record advances persisted state.db qty but NOT the in-memory running_net, so on a bucket mixing true-delta + absolute-target the rebuild and incremental folds seed the next target-differencing from different bases
description:
VERIFIED: fill_delta_normalizer.py:132-136 — a true-delta (non-absolute-target) record is passed through and explicitly does NOT advance net_map[key] (comment lines 133-135). But the incremental path (portfolio_state.py:643) seeds net from the PERSISTED positions row, which DID reflect the prior true-delta fill. So on a bucket mixing a true-delta fill (advances persisted qty, not in-memory running_net) and a later absolute-target fill, the rebuild fold's in-memory running_net and the incremental fold's persisted old_qty diverge as the carry-forward base for the next absolute-target record — the internal state.db split verdict.md attack (2) warned about, and exactly what the verdict.md:45 architectural parity gate must cover. DORMANT today (every historical record is absolute-target, schema_version absent), so this is correctness-hardening (add the mixed-schema parity test + reconcile the advance rule), not an active money bug. NEW — distinct from verdict attack-2 (single-regime) and from candidate 5 (cross-flag-regime); this is cross-SCHEMA within the normalizer. || TEST LANDED 2026-06-13 (workflow wt13usy0p): added tests/state/test_normalizer_incremental_parity.py mixed-schema parity test (abs->true-delta->abs in one bucket); strict=True xfail RED-proves the divergence (incremental=0.05 vs rebuild=0.07) and will XPASS-fail loudly if the advance rule is ever reconciled. DORMANT (no producer emits a true-delta record; schema_version defaults None=absolute-target). The fold advance-rule reconciliation is DEFERRED (only matters once a true-delta producer exists, and is behind the default-OFF flag). Gap now gated by the xfail. || RECONCILE 2026-06-14: STATUS: mixed-schema parity TEST MERGED (strict-xfail RED-proves the divergence + tripwires the reconciliation). The fold advance-rule FIX is DEFERRED (DORMANT — no producer emits a true-delta record; only matters once one exists, behind the default-OFF normalizer flag). Stays OPEN, dormant-gated.

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-15 (commit 76ed6ee). FillDeltaNormalizer's true-delta branch now advances the in-memory running_net by its delta (the persisted fold always did), so a mixed-schema bucket no longer diverges rebuild-vs-incremental on the carry-forward base. DORMANT today (all records absolute-target); flag-OFF + all-absolute byte-identical.

title: pdr_core AnalystView accepts bool for direction/magnitude/confidence and enforces neither bar_ts <= asof_decision (no-lookahead) nor the AssetClass Literal — contract over-promises vs __post_init__
description:
VERIFIED: AnalystView(direction=True, magnitude=True, asset_class='banana', bar_ts='2099-01-01', asof_decision='2020-01-01') constructs without error. contracts.py:134-150 __post_init__ validates direction membership and magnitude/confidence/confidence_raw finiteness+range but does NOT reject bool (int subclass, True passes `in (-1,0,1)`), does NOT validate asset_class against the Literal (line 47), and does NOT enforce the documented no-lookahead bar_ts<=asof_decision invariant (docstring lines 110-111). Timestamps are typed Any with a comment (lines 115-117) that the core never parses them — so the no-lookahead claim is aspirational, not enforced. Lower severity than the Fill/purity findings because the host shell currently validates upstream, but the contract is meant to be the trustworthy seam downstream stops re-validating, and a bool direction=True is a latent foot-gun for any `direction == 1` vs identity branch. The off-ladder float-rounding concern was CHECKED and is NOT a bug (_LADDER_ATOL=1e-9 bands are tiny/non-overlapping; 0.075 correctly rejected). Tighten when the deterministic leaves port (steps 3-6). NEW.

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-15 (commit d1c9bd8). AnalystView.__post_init__ now rejects bool for direction/magnitude/confidence/confidence_raw (isinstance bool guard before the int/float checks), closing the bool-subclass-of-int hole where True passed direction in (-1,0,1) and float(True)=1.0 passed the [0,1] range. Valid int/float byte-identical. NEW cs82 (Proposal/Fill have the same bool hole).

title: LIVE: portfolio_loader.reconstruct_portfolio reads a DEAD execution schema (schema_version==1 int + rec['qty']/['side']) that NO current producer emits — the enabled quant-playbook-weekly exit cron silently reconstructs an EMPTY portfolio and skips every stop/time-exit/LEAPS-dd close
description: VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE BUS (~/.hermes/quant/executions.jsonl, 46 records): every record carries schema_version=None, side=None, qty=None, target_position_pct=<frac> (e.g. -0.2). But daemon/portfolio_loader.py:76 filters `r.get('schema_version') == 1` (INTEGER) AND the loop body reads `rec['qty']` / `rec['side']` (lines 91-92). The live ExecutionRecord (react/base.py:89) defaults schema_version to None (or the STRING 'absolute-target-v1' when stamped) and emits target_position_pct/fill_size_pct via _record_to_dict (react/paper.py:56-79) — it has NO qty/side/schema_version==1 fields. So against live data the filter drops EVERY record => matching==[] => pf.positions empty. reconstruct_portfolio is LIVE: scripts/quant-playbook-weekly.py:296 (ENABLED cron, 30 6 * * 1). On empty positions the weekly hits the `not pf.positions` early-return (line 397, event=weekly_empty_portfolio) => NO -25% stop / time-exit / LEAPS-drawdown close EVER runs, even when the account holds a real short/long book. This ALSO makes cs00 (short-PnL sign) and cs01 (fail-open breakers) UNREACHABLE in prod (no record survives the filter to reach the close branch). The loader was written against an OLD/aspirational execution schema (the docstring at lines 9-24 shows the dead {qty,side,schema_version:1,realized_pnl} shape). FIX: accept None or SCHEMA_ABSOLUTE_TARGET (reuse react.base.is_absolute_target_record) AND translate target_position_pct->qty/side (the loader must consume the SAME record shape the reactors actually write, or be re-pointed at reconstruct_portfolio_state which already does). Add a regression test that feeds a REAL _record_to_dict() record through reconstruct_portfolio and asserts a non-empty book. CLASSIFY: the weekly exit cron is the live consumer; this is the highest-severity finding of the 2026-06-13 money-state increment. Distinct from cs00/cs01 (same file, different defect: those are the math, this is that the math is never reached). NEW (concurrent critique, workflow wt13usy0p). || INVESTIGATE-THEN-RECOMMEND COMPLETE 2026-06-14 (workflow wvd8kqpcp, orchestrator-verified: RED proof re-run 3 passed+1 xfailed, git diff confirms ZERO live-path .py edited, critique P1 verified on live bus). RED PROOF LANDED: tests/unit/test_weekly_exit_empty_book.py feeds a REAL ExecutionRecord->_record_to_dict record (not the masking schema_version==1 fake the old loader tests use), pins all three holes (HOLE-0 absent account_id, HOLE-1 schema_version None!=int 1, HOLE-2 loop reads rec['side']/['qty']), + a strict-xfail tripwire (test_green_live_record_reconstructs_one_position) that XPASS-fails when the fix lands. DECISION DOC: docs/design/2026-06-13-cs14-weekly-exit-reader-fork.md scores both fix shapes on 6 axes. RECOMMENDATION = OPTION B (fix daemon/portfolio_loader.reconstruct_portfolio in place): both options add the SAME enrichment (entry price+mark+share qty derived from the target_position_pct fraction), but B keeps the money-math single-sourced + preserves the weekly's Mapping[str,Position] contract with zero shim + makes cs00/cs01 reachable; A forces a new untested cost-basis shim onto the cron duplicating cs00 sign logic. Consumer-delta: the weekly reads pos.avg_entry_price/mark_price/qty which fraction-only reconstruct_portfolio_state cannot supply. The FIX (Seeds B1 admission-filter + B2 fraction->qty/side derivation) + the cs17 companion readers is DEFERRED to a later OPERATOR-APPROVED increment (operator chose investigate-then-recommend). Keep OPEN pending operator approval of Option B. || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 4d5cc42, squash-merge of inc/cs14-loader-fix, Option B). The loader now consumes the real producer shape via an additive absolute-target path (legacy/cs00/gate byte-unchanged); strict-xfail flipped to a real PASS; 65-test combined verification green. The mid-flight critique catch (a paper-only filter would drop 13/46 live det-equity/alpaca records) was FOLDED INTO the fix (EQUITY_FILL_REACTORS admission), so the earlier cs18-adjacent 'dropped det-equity' concern is RESOLVED in cs14 itself. Reachability follow-ons filed: cs20(P1 long-only exit math)/cs21(P3 fire-close)/cs22(P2 entry-basis)/cs23(P3 NAV).

title: Short positions inflate equity_total via abs(quantity) valuation in PortfolioState (reconstruct_from:538 + apply_execution:818) — proceeds enter cash AND abs-notional adds on top => ~2x|notional| NAV inflation feeding share-sizing
description: VERIFIED: portfolio_state.py:538-539 (reconstruct_from) and :818-819 (apply_execution) compute equity = cash + sum(abs(quantity) * avg_entry_price * mult). A SHORT fill already increases cash (proceeds; cash delta from a short open is positive), then abs(qty)*price ADDS the position notional ON TOP => the short leg is double-counted. Numeric proof from the critique: short 0.2 @ 100 from 100k => cash 100_020, equity_total 100_040 (should be ~100_000); inflation ~= 2x|notional|. CONSUMER: _account_nav_usd (react/paper.py) reads cash.equity_total and feeds it to the admissibility share-conversion NAV and the mirrored autonomous-tick NAV => oversized share counts on a book holding shorts. MITIGANTS (why P2 not P1): equity shorts are blocked by admissibility (ADR-0077, default-OFF) and the legacy NAV-fraction sizing path is the default; the inflation bites only once a short equity position is actually held AND share-conversion sizing is on. FIX: value the position at SIGNED qty net of buyback liability (a short is a liability, not an asset), not abs(); i.e. marked equity = cash + sum(signed_qty * (mark - avg_entry) ... ) or the correct net-liquidation formula. CLASSIFY test-only/defer: it changes a NAV number consumed by sizing => ship a RED-proving test documenting the inflation first; land the formula fix behind its own parity-tested increment (same posture as cr04/cr05). Distinct from cs00 (portfolio_loader realized-PnL) — this is portfolio_state equity_total. NEW (concurrent critique, workflow wt13usy0p). || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 59ffdb9). equity_total signed net-liq via _equity_qty_factor (a short is a liability, NAV-neutral at entry), flag-gated default-OFF behind HERMES_QUANT_SIGNED_EQUITY (gate-sized NAV -> live flip deferred to eval-gate). Flag-OFF returns abs() = bit-for-bit current on every book (verified on the live factor). us_option mult + abs membership filter preserved; long byte-identical; rebuild==incremental parity; 135-test combined verification green. This closes the MISSED HALF of ADR-0086 Phase 1 (the abs-sign fix that only landed in cash-delta + read-time get_marked_equity, never the cached equity_total). Residual: cs31/cs32 (get_marked_equity unit-basis + label).

title: LIVE safety-rail undercount: max_concurrent_positions + portfolio-caps read reconstruct_portfolio_state with the DEFAULT reactor_filter='paper', blind to deterministic-equity + alpaca_paper fills — counts 1 open where the live book holds 3
description: VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE BUS (~/.hermes/quant/executions.jsonl, 46 records). autonomous.py calls reconstruct_portfolio_state() for the ADR-0016 D9 max_concurrent_positions HARD safety rail (autonomous.py:497 'this is a hard safety rail, not a sizing refinement, so it is always on') AND for the portfolio-caps gate (autonomous.py:538). reconstruct_portfolio_state (portfolio/state.py:40) DEFAULTS reactor_filter='paper' (matches ONLY reactor_name=='paper'), and the autonomous call sites do NOT override it. But select_reactor (react/dispatch.py) routes equity fills to reactor_name 'deterministic-equity' (HERMES_QUANT_DETERMINISTIC_EQUITY=1) and 'alpaca_paper' (HERMES_QUANT_ALPACA_PAPER=1) — both armed on the live box. EMPIRICAL PROOF (this bus): reactor_filter='paper' => 1 open position (BA); reactor_filter=None => 3 open (BA + T via alpaca_paper + AAPL via deterministic-equity). reactor_name distribution on the bus: {paper:33, deterministic-equity:12, alpaca_paper:1}. So the 'always-on' max_concurrent_positions rail counts 1 where the real open book is 3 => the autonomous tick can open MORE positions than the rail permits — a hard safety rail silently degraded by reactor-name drift (the det-equity/alpaca share migration shipped+armed but this consumer still assumes only 'paper'). Same incident class as cr00/cr01 (det-equity migration shipped, consumers not updated). FIX (LATER increment): the open-book safety rail + caps gate must read the WHOLE book (reactor_filter=None) or an explicit set of ALL equity-fill reactor names, not just 'paper'. Distinct from cs14 (daemon portfolio_loader schema filter), cr04 (cross-symbol gross-cap race), ra10 (tick-lock). NEW (concurrent critique, workflow wvd8kqpcp, orchestrator-verified on the live bus). || FIX VERIFIED 2026-06-14 (workflow wp20n1d51 in worktree inc/cs16-safety-rail, orchestrator re-ran 26 tests GREEN from the worktree root + confirmed import shadows the worktree source). Prove confirmed: reactor_filter='paper' undercounts (1 of 3 open on the live bus); reactor_filter=None is the TRUE book and is fail-CLOSED-safe; NO double-count risk (reconstruct keys by asset alone => collapses); override-at-call-site (NOT change-default, which a test locks). FIX: reactor_filter=None at autonomous.py:523 (D9 rail) + :548 (caps gate); portfolio/state.py default unchanged; + RED->GREEN source-bound test (tests/unit/test_concurrent_rail_counts_whole_book.py). PENDING squash-merge onto docs/rearchitecture-shared-pdr-core (sequenced after cs14). FOLLOW-ON: cs18 (account-partition the reader so the fix doesn't pool the alpaca-paper shadow book) + cs19 (rail fail-open-to-0). || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 2f1a280, squash-merge of inc/cs16-safety-rail). reactor_filter=None at both rail call sites; 65-test combined verification green on the merged tree. Follow-ons cs18(P1)/cs19(P2) remain open.

title: Weekly-exit raw-executions readers (infer_play_tag / find_entry_record / days_between_iso) read rec['side']=='buy' + rec['asof'] — both ABSENT on live records; play_tag defaults 'swing' for all + entry-context returns None -> ERROR/HOLD
description: VERIFIED (companion of cs14, same root cause, fixed by NEITHER cs14 option): beyond the empty-Portfolio hole, the weekly ALSO reads the RAW executions list (second return of load_portfolio, read_jsonl_tail direct, quant-playbook-weekly.py:293). infer_play_tag (weekly:204-226) gates on rec['side']=='buy' (line 216) — 'side' is ABSENT on live records (the live ExecutionRecord emits target_position_pct, not side/qty; see cs14), so the guard continues every record and play_tag silently defaults to 'swing' for ALL positions. find_entry_record (weekly:230-235) gates on rec['side']=='buy' then reads the entry rec's rec['asof'] for days_held (weekly:460) — both 'side' and 'asof' are absent on live records (live shape uses asof_execution), so it returns None => weekly:430 logs ERROR 'no opening execution found' and HOLDs. Apply to BOTH scripts/quant-playbook-weekly.py AND the identical ops/scripts/quant-playbook-weekly.py twin (deploy-sync drift). NEW (concurrent critique + Prove deep-dive, workflow wvd8kqpcp). See docs/design/2026-06-13-cs14-weekly-exit-reader-fork.md §4. || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 4d5cc42, with cs14). _rec_side derives side from sign(target_position_pct); infer_play_tag/find_entry_record use it; entry-ts reads asof_execution->asof; applied to BOTH byte-identical weekly twins (diff empty).
