description: VERIFIED genuinely-new (cs27 critique). ADR-0035 §98 requires the take-profit threshold to use ATR-14_AT_ENTRY; the dataclass field encodes it (SwingContext.atr14_at_entry_pct, scripts/quant-playbook-weekly.py:145) and decide_swing's TP rule is tp_threshold = SWING_TP_ATR_MULT * ctx.atr14_at_entry_pct (weekly:168-169). BUT fetch_mark_atr (weekly:393-400) computes the CURRENT ATR: t.history(period='60d') ends TODAY, close=h['Close'].iloc[-1] (today's close), atr=tr.tail(14).mean(); its own docstring says 'atr14_pct_at_recent_close' (weekly:381). run_weekly wires this CURRENT atr into the AT-ENTRY field: mark, atr_pct = fetch_mark_atr(asset) (weekly:539) -> decide_swing(SwingContext(..., atr14_at_entry_pct=atr_pct or 0.0)) (weekly:573). IMPACT: the 3xATR take-profit fires against TODAY's vol regime, not entry-time — too early if vol fell since entry (threshold shrank), too late if vol spiked. ORTHOGONAL to cs27/cs28 (which fix WHICH leg supplies days_held/play): even with the correct establishing leg, the ATR still comes from today's window. SHORT-SPECIFIC 2nd-order (cs20 interaction): for a short pnl_pct=(avg_entry-mark)/avg_entry but atr_pct=atr/close uses the CURRENT mark as denominator — as a short profits (mark falls) the atr_pct denominator shrinks, inflating the TP threshold, making a deeply-profitable short HARDER to take-profit. FIX: compute ATR over the window ENDING at the establishing-leg date (now available post-cs27) and divide by the entry-date close, not today's. BEST LANDED NOW (cs27 made the establishing-leg date reliably available). Standing bug since file creation. DRY-RUN default. NEW (cs27 concurrent critique, workflow waf19tg7q, orchestrator-verified). || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 90faa28). fetch_mark_atr gained optional entry_date: ATR-14 window ending at the cs27 establishing-leg date + entry-date close denominator (ADR-0035 §98), removing both the regime drift and the cs20 short atr/mark denominator drift. entry_date=None byte-identical; layered no-fabrication fallback to recent-ATR + journal atr_basis marker. Stable-vol single-fill-long TP ~unchanged; both twins identical; 55-test combined verification green.

title: Weekly days_between_iso guards only `except ValueError`, so a non-str asof_execution/asof (numeric epoch / null / pd.Timestamp leak) raises uncaught AttributeError/TypeError, killing the per-asset loop / whole run
description: VERIFIED at scripts/quant-playbook-weekly.py:313-322. days_between_iso does `s = asof_iso.replace('Z','+00:00')` then datetime.fromisoformat(s), wrapped ONLY by `except ValueError: return 0`. If asof_iso is not a str, .replace raises AttributeError (numeric/None) or fromisoformat raises TypeError — neither caught. Caller (weekly:535-536) passes entry.get('asof_execution') or entry.get('asof',''). asof_execution is typed str (react/base.py:61) so the LIVE bus is safe TODAY; the docstring claims 'Robust to ISO with or without Z' but it is NOT robust to non-str input. A malformed/legacy/settlement record with a numeric or null asof_execution would raise an uncaught exception that propagates out of the per-asset loop -> main()'s catch-all logs weekly_uncaught_exception and returns 1 -> NO decisions for the WHOLE run (silence-by-default hides it). P3: defensive-only, low probability given typed producers, no money-state corruption — but a single bad bus line silently disables the entire weekly rebalance. FIX: widen to `except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError)` or coerce str(asof_iso) before parsing. NOT cs27/cs28. NEW (cs27 concurrent critique, workflow waf19tg7q). Cheap to fold into the cs29 increment (same file). || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 90faa28, with cs29). days_between_iso widened to `except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError): return 0` — a non-str asof now degrades that position to days_held=0 instead of aborting the whole weekly run via main's catch-all. str-ISO happy path byte-identical.

title: get_marked_equity treats true-shares/contract positions as NAV-fractions: MTM off by nav_ref (and the option contract-multiplier) — orphaned read-time API, no live caller
description:
VERIFIED (cs15 critique): portfolio_state.py:954 get_marked_equity computes unrealized_i = pos.quantity * nav_ref * (mark/avg_entry - 1.0), hardcoding the NAV-FRACTION basis (docstring :926). But the two write folds (_apply_execution_unsafe :639-662, _replay_record :1137-1149) branch on reactor_metadata.quantity (leg_quantity): multi-leg/Alpaca positions persist quantity in REAL SHARES/CONTRACTS (the cr00/cr01 unit-basis split), NOT a NAV fraction. get_marked_equity does NOT branch on unit. Traced: long 50sh @100, mark 110, nav_ref 100000 -> current 50*100000*(110/100-1)=500,000 vs correct real-shares MTM 50*(110-100)=500 (off by ~nav_ref, ~1000x here); us_option ALSO omits _CONTRACT_MULTIPLIER (another 100x). DISTINCT from cs15 (equity_total cost-basis SIGN; the get_marked_equity SHORT SIGN is verified CORRECT: short -0.2@100 -> mark 90 = +2000) and from cr00/cr01 (loader/cap-clip basis). P2 not P1: get_marked_equity has NO live production caller (only a comment at cli/status.py:595 + a do-NOT-wire note at react/paper.py:123) — an orphaned-but-built MTM instrument; the unit bug bleeds only once a true-shares book is fed to a WIRED marked-report surface. FIX: branch the MTM math on the same leg_quantity/true-unit predicate the folds use (real-shares: quantity*(mark-entry)*contract_multiplier; NAV-fraction: keep quantity*nav_ref*(mark/entry-1)), preserving the short sign. NEW (cs15 concurrent critique, workflow w2znwt0w7). Check orphan-status (is it ever wired?) before building — same orphaned-instrument lesson. || ANALYSIS DONE, MERGE SCOPE-REJECTED 2026-06-14 (workflow wvmfbf83f). A B2 workflow PROVED the read-time unit is not recoverable without persistence (see cs33) and IMPLEMENTED the correct fix (qty_unit column + idempotent ALTER TABLE migration + both write folds stamp it + branched MTM; short sign preserved; nav-fraction byte-identical; 21+70 tests green). The orchestrator REJECTED the merge on SCOPE: get_marked_equity is ORPHANED (no live caller), so a live state.db SCHEMA MIGRATION + relaxing the restate read-only DDL guarantee to fix a bug nothing consumes is the wrong trade. Validated implementation + RED tests preserved at docs/design/2026-06-14-cs31-marked-equity-unit-analysis.md. RE-SCOPE: land cs31 (MTM branch) + cs33 (qty_unit schema column) TOGETHER as a dedicated, separately-reviewed increment WHEN get_marked_equity is wired to a live marked-report surface OR an operator approves the schema migration on its own merits. Stays OPEN (re-scoped, not abandoned). The correctness analysis is the durable deliverable; the live-money schema change is deferred to a justified trigger.

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-15 (commit f615fc0). get_marked_equity now derives the MTM unit from the persisted asset_class (us_option -> ×100 contract × (mark-avg); equity/legacy -> the unchanged NAV-fraction basis), fixing the ~500x us_option overstatement. NO migration (asset_class is in the positions PK). Legacy book byte-identical.

title: get_marked_equity equity_basis flag can never report 'mark' when an invalid-avg position is present (label artifact, not a money number)
description:
VERIFIED (cs15 critique): portfolio_state.py:947 skips positions with avg_entry_price<=0 via `continue` (so they never increment n_marked), but :961 sets n_positions = len(positions) INCLUDING the skipped one. A book with one bad-avg position can therefore never satisfy n_marked==n_positions, so equity_basis collapses to 'mixed' even when every VALID position is marked. Affects only the reporting-flag label (MarkedEquity.equity_basis), NOT marked_equity/total_unrealized money figures. Low-stakes; fold into the cs31 unit-fix (same function) or skip. NOT cs15/cr00/cr01. NEW (cs15 concurrent critique, workflow w2znwt0w7). || ANALYSIS DONE, BUNDLED-WITH-cs31 2026-06-14 (workflow wvmfbf83f). The n_positions-counts-skipped-rows label fix (use n_considered as the denominator) was implemented + tested green in the same workflow, but rides the same orphaned-get_marked_equity merge the orchestrator scope-rejected (it edits the same function). Re-scoped to land WITH cs31/cs33 when get_marked_equity is wired/approved. Trivial (reporting-label only, no money figure); captured in docs/design/2026-06-14-cs31-marked-equity-unit-analysis.md.

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-15 (commit f615fc0). get_marked_equity now counts only CONSIDERED positions (avg>0) in the equity_basis denominator, so a one-bad-avg book can read 'mark' when every valid position is marked (was: n_positions=len counted the skipped row -> always 'mixed').

title: get_marked_equity cannot recover position UNIT at read time (positions table persists no unit flag) — a true-shares row and a NAV-fraction row are byte-identical, so the cs31 MTM fix needs a schema column, NOT a read-time re-derivation
description:
VERIFIED (cs31 Prove + critique, analysis preserved at docs/design/2026-06-14-cs31-marked-equity-unit-analysis.md): the positions table schema (portfolio_state.py:175-183) stores ONLY {account_id, asset_class, symbol, quantity, avg_entry_price, last_update_at} — NO unit flag. The write folds discriminate real-shares vs NAV-fraction by reactor_metadata.quantity PRESENCE at write time (_apply_execution_unsafe :681-683 leg_quantity), but that signal is CONSUMED and never persisted; only the resulting quantity lands in the row. asset_class does NOT discriminate (multileg/alpaca write real-shares rows with asset_class='equity', same as the legacy NAV-fraction paper path). So get_marked_equity literally cannot branch on the write-fold unit predicate — a 50-share equity long and a 0.5 NAV-fraction equity long are indistinguishable rows. The honest fix REQUIRES persistence (a qty_unit column + a migration on the live state.db) OR a caller-supplied unit policy — NOT a read-time heuristic. DISPOSITION 2026-06-14: a cs31 workflow PROVED + IMPLEMENTED exactly this (qty_unit column + idempotent ALTER TABLE + both write folds stamp it + branched MTM), all tests green — BUT the orchestrator REJECTED the merge: get_marked_equity is ORPHANED (no live caller), so paying a live money-state SCHEMA MIGRATION + relaxing the restate read-only DDL guarantee (test_restate_does_not_mutate_state_db) to fix a bug nothing consumes is the wrong trade. The schema migration is a real money-state change that deserves its own reviewed increment, NOT a rider on an orphaned read-API fix. ROUTE: fix cs31's MTM (cs31 stays open) TOGETHER with this schema column AS A DEDICATED increment WHEN get_marked_equity is actually wired to a live marked-report surface (or when an operator approves the schema migration on its own merits). The validated implementation + RED tests are captured in the design doc for fast re-land. NEW (cs31 concurrent critique, workflow wvmfbf83f, orchestrator scope-rejected the merge).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-15 (commit f615fc0). the position UNIT is recovered at read time from the persisted asset_class column (in the PK) — NO qty_unit schema migration needed (the original cs31 scope-reject premise is obsolete; asset_class suffices for the us_option ×100 discriminator). NOTE follow-up cs82: equity-row unit (fractional shares vs NAV-fraction) is NOT asset_class-recoverable, but only us_option needs the multiplier branch; equity keeps the byte-identical legacy basis.

title: get_marked_equity does not validate mark finiteness/positivity: a NaN mark NaNs the whole account equity snapshot; a 0/negative mark books a >=100% phantom loss
description:
VERIFIED (cs31 critique): portfolio_state.py:996-1000 does mark = mark_prices.get(pos.symbol); if mark is not None: unrealized = quantity*nav_ref*(mark/avg_entry-1.0). ONLY `is not None` is checked — no isfinite/positivity guard. A NaN mark -> unrealized NaN -> total_unrealized NaN -> marked_equity NaN (one bad symbol poisons the WHOLE account equity figure) while n_marked still increments (so equity_basis can read 'mark' on a NaN book). A 0.0 mark -> mark/entry-1 = -1 -> full -100% on that leg; negative -> >100% loss. DISTINCT from cr05 (which rejects zero/negative DECISION price in the WRITE/PaperReactor path; this is the READ-path injected MARK, not covered by cr05's guard). Orphaned read-time API (no live caller) so LATENT, but bleeds the instant a marked-report surface feeds a mark dict that can contain NaN/0/neg (e.g. a yfinance fetch miss returning NaN). FIX: skip or refuse non-finite/<=0 marks (fall back to entry / contribute 0), the same fail-closed posture as the equity/options gates (cr02/cs06). Best fixed WITH cs31/cs33 (same function). NEW (cs31 concurrent critique, workflow wvmfbf83f).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-15 (commit f615fc0). get_marked_equity now guards mark isfinite + >0 (skip the leg + do NOT count it), so a NaN/0/negative mark no longer poisons the whole-account marked_equity to NaN.

title: get_marked_equity looks up marks by symbol ONLY, ignoring asset_class: an equity and a us_option on the same underlying receive the same mark (cross-asset-class mark bleed)
description:
VERIFIED (cs31 critique): positions PK is (account_id, asset_class, symbol) (schema :182), but get_marked_equity does mark_prices.get(pos.symbol) at :996, DROPPING asset_class from the lookup. A book holding an equity position and a us_option position whose symbol resolves to the same underlying both receive the SAME value from mark_prices[symbol] — an equity share price applied to an option premium (or vice versa), producing a wildly wrong unrealized on at least one leg. The marks dict must be keyed (asset_class, symbol) to match the positions PK. DISTINCT from ac1 (the 'option' vs 'us_option' multiplier STRING divergence, not the mark-lookup key) and from cs31 (unit basis). Orphaned read-time API so LATENT; P3 because it only bites a book holding BOTH an equity and an option on the same symbol with a flat mark dict. FIX: key mark_prices by (asset_class, symbol). Best fixed WITH cs31/cs33/cs34 (same function). NEW (cs31 concurrent critique, workflow wvmfbf83f).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-15 (commit f615fc0). get_marked_equity now keys the mark lookup on (asset_class, symbol) with a symbol-only fallback, so a same-underlying equity + us_option no longer receive the same mark.

title: Weekly close path never plumbs a close decision_price into the fire — _fire_equity_close builds a Proposal with decision_price=0.0 sentinel -> v0.2 slippage degrades the close fill to fill_price=0.0 (cr05 path)
description:
VERIFIED (cs21 critique): run_weekly already fetches `mark` for the exit-rule math (fetch_mark_atr) but _fire_equity_close is invoked with ONLY (symbol, qty, target_position_pct, reason) — no decision_price/mark threaded in. The cs21-built Proposal carries advisor_result with decision_price best-effort 0.0, so paper.py _extract_decision_price returns the 0.0 sentinel. With HERMES_QUANT_PAPER_SLIPPAGE_MODEL defaulting to v0.2, apply_slippage raises ValueError on decision_price<=0 and the reactor degrades to fill_price=0.0 (the cr05 corrupt-record branch). DISTINCT from cr05 (the generic reactor degrade-vs-reject decision): this is that the WEEKLY close path has NO close-price plumbing — it should thread the `mark` it already holds into the Proposal's advisor_result.decision_price. P3: downstream of the armed path (DRY-RUN default), fails toward a 0-price audit record not a mis-fire. FIX: thread the weekly's already-fetched mark into _fire_equity_close -> advisor_result['decision_price']. NEW (cs21 concurrent critique, workflow w110bpr0c).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-15 (commit 24f5575). the weekly close fire now plumbs the symbol mark as decision_price (the same last_close source the daily close uses); post-cr05 it FILLS at a real price instead of silently no-filling on the 0.0 sentinel. A missing/<=0 mark still fail-closes per cr05.

title: Weekly options-leg detection `len(asset) > 6` silently HOLDs any equity ticker longer than 6 chars (skips its exit gate)
description:
VERIFIED (cs21 critique): scripts/quant-playbook-weekly.py:611 `if ' ' in asset or len(asset) > 6:` routes the symbol to options_skipped + TODO_ADR0029 continue. The space check is a sound OCC-symbol heuristic, but `len(asset) > 6` ALSO trips on any legitimate equity symbol >6 chars (multi-class ADR/ETF tickers, 7-char symbols) — such a held equity position is silently classified as an option-leg and HELD forever (its swing/leaps 60d/-25% exit rules never run). P3: no equity >6 chars in the current ADR-0035 universe, but it is a silent false-HOLD suppressing the exit gate on an otherwise-managed position. FIX: detect options by the OCC space/shape (or an explicit options-symbol predicate), not raw length. Apply to BOTH weekly twins. NEW (cs21 concurrent critique, workflow w110bpr0c).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-15 (commit 24f5575). weekly options-leg detection now uses parse_occ success (structural) instead of len(asset)>6, so a 7+char equity ticker (GOOG.OQ, ADRs) is no longer wrongly HELD as an option; degrades to the legacy len check on import failure.

title: OHLCV read-through cache (data/cache.py cached_fetch) returns most-recent bars on a warm cache HIT with no as_of/end predicate — backtest lookahead leak past the --end anchor
description: VERIFIED (cs11 critique, orchestrator-confirmed): hermes_quant/data/cache.py:117-156 cached_fetch — on a cache HIT (len(cached)>=min_hit_bars, :149) it returns `cached.tail(min(lookback_bars, len(cached)))` (:150) with NO as_of/end predicate (the function has no as_of or end parameter at all). OhlcvCache.read()->normalize_bars sorts ASCENDING by timestamp (cache.py:186), so .tail() returns the MOST-RECENT cached bars, which can post-date the current backtest's requested cutoff; the cache file accumulates bars up to each prior fetch's wall-clock via append. The as_of-aware fetch closure is invoked ONLY on a cache MISS (:158). WIRING: cli/__init__.py:1714 cached_fetch(fetch,...) wraps an inner fetch() (:1695) that DOES pass as_of=as_of derived from --end (cli:1610-1611 `as_of = pd.Timestamp(end) if end else None`) — but the as_of only applies on a MISS; on a warm HIT the tail bypasses it. So a backtest with --end<past date> against a warm cache (populated by an earlier fetch to a later date) is served bars AFTER --end -> inflated/optimistic OOS metrics on any cached symbol. P2 (not P1): cached_fetch is wired in the BACKTEST/research CLI fetch path (cli/__init__.py), NOT the live react/daemon tick path — but it is a no-lookahead charter-invariant violation in backtests. DISTINCT from cs04 (fetch_with_chain no-asof, closed), cs05 (horizon_cache resample clip, closed — DIFFERENT module), cs11 (AV provider range, fixed), cs12 (fundamentals). FIX: thread an as_of/end cutoff into cached_fetch and prune the returned tail to timestamp<=cutoff on the HIT path (and gate the hit on having enough bars AT-OR-BEFORE the cutoff, not just enough total). NEW (cs11 concurrent critique, workflow wbcj8nt0n). || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 8c07117). cached_fetch gained a cutoff kwarg (threaded from the CLI --end-derived as_of): the warm-HIT path prunes the returned tail to timestamp<=cutoff AND gates the hit on enough bars AT-OR-BEFORE the cutoff (not total — a future-only cache now falls through to a real fetch instead of serving too-few past bars); the MISS merge also post-prunes. cutoff=None (live/up-to-now caller) prunes nothing = BYTE-IDENTICAL. Closes the warm-cache lookahead leak (a backtest --end<past> against a cache populated later was served FUTURE bars). Only the backtest CLI fetch path calls cached_fetch (no live tick — grep-verified). 11 tests green (3 new: hit-prune, at-or-before-gate, cutoff=None byte-identical). NEW critique cs43 (right-edge staleness: the gate counts but doesn't bound newest-bar-near-cutoff).

title: validation.py excess-return path subtracts DATE-MISALIGNED bars: strat/bh finite-filtered independently (compressing each) then subtracted positionally (r[:m]-bh[:m]) — a non-finite at different indices shifts the arrays and corrupts the excess permutation test + bootstrap CI feeding the promotion gate
description: VERIFIED (cs08 critique): hermes_quant/evaluation/validation.py _to_array (L183) does arr[np.isfinite(arr)] which DROPS non-finite ELEMENTS and COMPRESSES the array. validate_returns coerces strat_returns (L485) and bh_returns (L572) INDEPENDENTLY, then forms the excess positionally: excess = r[:m] - bh[:m] (L575). If strat and bh have a non-finite element at DIFFERENT indices (a halt/gap in one series but not the other), the two arrays shift relative to each other and the subtraction pairs bars from DIFFERENT DATES. DEMONSTRATED: strat=[.01,.02,.03,.04,.05], bh=[.01,NaN,.02,.03,.04] -> bh compresses to [.01,.02,.03,.04], excess=[0,.01,.01,.01] (date-misaligned) instead of the true paired excess. This corrupts the excess-return permutation test + the excess_return bootstrap CI written to validation.json — which feeds the paper->live PROMOTION gate. LATENT today (pct_change().dropna() usually leaves both series finite at the same indices), but MORE LIKELY once cs11/cs12 provider work changes which bars are present/NaN. No existing seed covers it. FIX: align strat/bh by a shared timestamp index (or mask non-finite on the UNION and drop paired) BEFORE the positional subtract, so excess pairs same-date bars. NEW (cs08 concurrent critique, workflow w100p5eyo). || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 3c0baaf). Added _paired_finite(a,b) to validation.py: coerces strat/bh and aligns them on a SHARED finite mask (isfinite(a)&isfinite(b) over the common length) so a non-finite in EITHER drops that bar from BOTH -> the excess subtract pairs same-date bars. The excess block re-coerces from the ORIGINAL strat_returns via _paired_finite (not the independently-compressed r); the strat-only r + ALL per-series stats (Sharpe/DSR/timing-perm/sharpe-CI/n-guards) UNTOUCHED. All-finite case BYTE-IDENTICAL (joint mask all-True -> excess==r[:m]-bh[:m], np.array_equal verified). Closes the date-misalignment that corrupted the timing_excess permutation test (order-sensitive _timing_pnl) + the excess_return bootstrap CI in validation.json — the OOS evidence the paper->live promotion gate trusts. RED->GREEN (misaligned-NaN now yields the hand-computed paired excess; all-finite unchanged); 19 tests green; validation.py only. NEW critique cs46 (inf bootstrap-sharpe samples -> NaN promotion-gate CI).

title: FundamentalsAnalyst 7-day fetched_at staleness gate and the 45-day reporting lag are mutually exclusive on a sparse backtest cache -> silent total abstention
description: VERIFIED (cs12 critique): analysts/fundamentals.py:222-223 abstains when age_days=(asof-fetched_at).days > _STALENESS_DAYS_HARD_LIMIT (7). But a lag-gated row (post-cs12) only becomes VISIBLE at period_end+45d, while fetched_at ~= the cache day near period_end — so by the time the 45d lag admits the row, its fetched_at is ~30d+ old and the 7d staleness gate REJECTS it. On any backtest cache not re-snapshotted daily (the exact no-lookahead replay path B34/cs12 target), the two no-lookahead controls CANCEL and FundamentalsAnalyst emits ZERO views. Live steady-state masks it (the cron writes a fresh fetched_at row daily). FIX: the staleness gate should key off as_of_date / the knowable date, not fetched_at, once the lag filter is authoritative. Distinct from cs12 (the lag default) — this is the staleness gate interacting with it. NEW (cs12 concurrent critique, workflow wvdb6ms9u). || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 0f0e7f9). Two-axis staleness gate in fundamentals.py: (1) DATUM-recency vs the fiscal-period basis (report_date preferred else period_end — same precedence as the provider's _apply_reporting_lag_filter) with a cadence-aware _STALENESS_DATUM_DAYS_HARD_LIMIT=190 (~2 quarters); (2) the 7d fetched_at limit RETAINED only as a cron-liveness FALLBACK for basis-LESS old-schema/pre-B34 NaT rows. This stops the cs12-lag × 7d-fetched_at CANCELLATION that darkened the FundamentalsAnalyst universe-wide on a sparse backtest cache (a lag-admitted row at period_end+45d was rejected by the 7d gate because fetched_at was ~30d old). SAFETY: restores a wrongly-dark input (no signal invented); the no-lookahead lag filter is UNTOUCHED + still ANDed at read_latest; a genuinely-stale row (period_end >~2 quarters old) is STILL rejected on the datum axis (no flag needed — cannot admit data the lag filter excludes). Test #9 rewritten from period_end=2025-12-31 (only 90d, NOT stale) to a genuinely-stale period to keep asserting abstain — the proof the gate moved to content-age not cache-age. 17 tests green; provider/cs12 untouched. cs40's own critique candidate was is_new=False (re-described cs40).

title: read_sector_median_pe has NO reporting-lag filter (asymmetry with read_latest): the sector P/E benchmark can embed not-yet-public constituent fundamentals in a backtest
description:
VERIFIED (cs12 critique): fundamentals_provider.py:406-459 read_sector_median_pe filters ONLY `as_of_date <= as_of` and never calls _apply_reporting_lag_filter, while its sibling read_latest (the SAME analyst's other input) now applies the lag post-cs12. refresh_sector_medians (:571) builds the median from read_latest(ticker) with as_of=None (latest snapshot, no lag) then stamps as_of_date=now, so a backtest read of the historical sector median can incorporate fundamentals not yet public. Worst-case bounded by as_of_date so lower acuity than the per-ticker leak, but a clear lookahead ASYMMETRY on the analyst's pe_relative sub-signal that cs12 leaves open. FIX: apply the same reporting-lag filter to read_sector_median_pe (symmetry with read_latest). NEW (cs12 concurrent critique, workflow wvdb6ms9u).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 4aa9c2d). read_sector_median_pe now applies the SAME reporting-lag filter as read_latest (asymmetry closed): the sector-median PE sub-signal no longer leaks rows public-dated after as_of. Point-in-time integrity restored on the sector-relative axis.

title: read_latest returns newest-by-fetched_at with no fetched_at<=as_of guard; write_snapshot dedupe (keep latest fetched_at per as_of_date) lets a backfill rewrite historical fundamentals (point-in-time integrity hole)
description:
VERIFIED (cs12 critique): fundamentals_provider.py:403-404 selects df.sort_values('fetched_at').iloc[-1] with NO fetched_at<=as_of constraint. (a) SAME-DAY: as_of_date=D (day-normalized) satisfies `<= as_of (D 00:00)` while fetched_at=D+12h > as_of, returning a row fetched in the FUTURE -> negative age_days that silently passes the analyst 7d staleness gate. (b) BACKFILL: write_snapshot dedupes on as_of_date keeping the latest fetched_at (:494-496) — a backfill re-fetch of an old as_of_date carrying TODAY's fetched_at REPLACES that historical row's fundamentals while keeping the old as_of_date, so a point-in-time read at the old date returns CURRENT values — a lookahead via backfill no filter catches. Point-in-time integrity hole independent of the reporting-lag work. FIX: add a fetched_at<=as_of guard in read_latest + a point-in-time-preserving dedupe (do not let a newer fetched_at overwrite an old as_of_date's values). NEW (cs12 concurrent critique, workflow wvdb6ms9u).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 4aa9c2d). read_latest now guards fetched_at<=as_of (newest-by-fetched_at no longer returns a row snapshotted AFTER the decision instant): point-in-time honesty on the fetched_at axis. No-lookahead charter invariant.

title: validation.py _percentile_ci: inf bootstrap-sharpe samples corrupt the promotion-gate CI (ci_low -> NaN on zero-variance resamples)
description:
VERIFIED end-to-end (cs39 critique): _sharpe (evaluation/validation.py:186) returns +/-math.inf when std(ddof=1)==0 and mean!=0 (a stationary-bootstrap resample can draw a single repeated block -> constant series -> zero variance). _percentile_ci (:337) uses np.nanpercentile, which drops NaN but KEEPS inf; when an inf sample lands in the tail-interpolation window, numpy's internal subtract(b,a) on inf yields NaN, corrupting ci_low/ci_high. REPRODUCED via the public API: validate_returns(np.array([0.001]*42), bars_per_year=252) -> sharpe ci_low=NaN, ci_high=NaN, point=inf. IMPACT: the 'sharpe' ci_low is the sharpe_95ci_lower the paper->live PROMOTION gate trusts (governance/promotion.py:274; react/live.py:38 requires >=1.0); a NaN/None lower bound on a degenerate/low-variance series changes gate behavior. DISTINCT from cs39 (excess date-misalignment, fixed). FIX: drop/replace non-finite (inf as well as NaN) bootstrap samples before _percentile_ci, OR guard _sharpe's inf branch to a finite sentinel for the resample distribution. Same file as cs39 (validation.py) — bundle with a validation-hardening follow-up. NEW (cs39 concurrent critique, workflow wo92vj79v).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 7620247). validation.py _percentile_ci now filters NON-FINITE bootstrap samples (NaN AND ±inf) before the percentile, then percentiles only the finite tail; a fully-degenerate (all non-finite) distribution returns a conservative finite (0.0,0.0) so the sharpe_95ci_lower<1.0 promotion gate fails-CLOSED instead of reading a NaN (NaN<1.0 is False -> a NaN CI silently PASSES). np.nanpercentile dropped NaN but KEPT inf, and a degenerate zero-variance resample makes _sharpe return ±inf. samples coerced via np.asarray (caller-shape-agnostic). title: deflated_sharpe / DSR path is NaN-on-inf (same inf-propagation class as cs46, on the DSR axis) — a degenerate ±inf Sharpe corrupts the DSR the promotion gate trusts
description:

title: reconstruct_from has NO dedup, so a true byte-duplicate fill (crash-in-window retry) double-counts on rebuild — the ledger-reconcile --apply path would 'heal' the correct deduped live book to an inflated NAV (inverse of cs51)

FIX: have reconstruct_from dedup byte-identical (proposal_id, asof_execution, asset, asset_class, leg_index) records in its accumulator the SAME way the incremental fold does (or seed/consult processed_fills), so the two folds agree on a crash-retry duplicate. title: cached_fetch cs43 staleness bound over-tightens for calendar-gapped markets: a fresh fully-supplied daily/intraday cache wrongly MISSes every weekend/holiday/overnight anchor -> refetch-forever loop
description:
VERIFIED (cs49+50 concurrent critique). cs43 (MERGED) set the right-edge bound to ONE literal timeframe step (cache.py _infer_step: 1d->1 day, 1h->1 hour, ZERO trading-calendar awareness). But non-24/7 markets have legitimate calendar gaps at the right edge: a DAILY equity cache's freshest real bar is Friday's close, yet a backtest --end anchored Monday (cutoff=as_of) sits ~3 calendar days above Friday > the 1-day bound -> the HIT is REJECTED even though the cache is fresh, contiguous, and the provider has nothing newer (markets closed Sat/Sun). PROBE (1d, Mon-Fri bars, Monday cutoff): MISS, gap 3 days, fetch_calls 1->2->3 across 3 runs -> REFETCH-FOREVER on the MOST COMMON backtest case. Same for INTRADAY over an overnight session gap (1h equity 14:00-20:00Z, next-00:00Z cutoff -> MISS, 4h>1h). A REGRESSION cs43 introduced; the cs43 tests only used 24/7-contiguous data so structurally could not catch it. P1: breaks the common daily/option backtest with a refetch loop (latency + provider hammering) on a correct cache. FIX (cache.py only, reuse cs43 _infer_step/bound, no new constant): judge right-edge freshness by whether the newest eligible bar advanced as far as the calendar/provider allows — tolerate the bound being exceeded when the cache's own trailing observed inter-bar spacing already shows comparable gaps (the trailing observed step, not the canonical one), OR widen the default bound to a small calendar multiple (covers a 3-day weekend) while still rejecting the multi-MONTH cs43 gap. Keep cutoff=None byte-identical, keep cs43's multi-month rejection + cs50 contiguity + cs49 short-circuit. Scope: data/cache.py only. NEW (cs49+50 critique).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 51e672e). cached_fetch now uses a self-calibrating _calendar_bound (learns the cache's own RECURRING inter-bar gap; max(canonical, largest_recurring)) for the right-edge freshness check at BOTH the HIT gate + the MISS abstain flag, fixing the cs43 regression where a fresh daily cache (Fri close) with a Monday --end MISSed+refetched every run. cs43 multi-month STILL MISS, cs50 interior hole STILL MISS, cs49 short-circuit intact, cutoff=None byte-identical. The COMMON weekend/overnight P1 harm is fixed; the rarer market-HOLIDAY case (gap recurs <2x) is deferred to cs63. 29 cache tests green.

title: write_sector_median lacks the cs42(b) cross-day-backfill PIT-preservation guard write_snapshot got — a re-fetch silently rewrites a historical sector-median value
description:

Closes the pe_relative-denominator PIT-mutation. 38 tests green.

title: _portfolio_cap_clip re-collapses (asset_class, symbol) -> bare symbol when building pos_map: a cap-accounting key narrowing (sibling of cs51) that can mis-aggregate same-symbol cross-asset-class exposure
description:
VERIFIED (cr04+cr05 concurrent critique). _portfolio_cap_clip builds its pos_map keyed on the bare SYMBOL while the canonical position key is (account, asset_class, symbol). When the same symbol exists under two asset_classes (e.g. an equity AND a us_option on the same underlying, or an equity + its delisted-then-relisted variant), the bare-symbol pos_map collapses the two distinct positions into one bucket, mis-aggregating the gross-exposure the cap clips against -> the cap can under- or over-count exposure for a same-symbol cross-asset-class book. Sibling of cs51 (per-leg dedup key too narrow) and cs35 (get_marked_equity symbol-only mark lookup ignoring asset_class) — the recurring symbol-vs-(asset_class,symbol) key-narrowing family. Gated on HERMES_QUANT_PORTFOLIO_CAPS=1. FIX: key pos_map on (asset_class, symbol) (or the full canonical key) so the cap accounts distinct same-symbol positions separately. Scope: react/paper.py only. NEW (cr04/cr05 critique).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit e55136d). _portfolio_cap_clip pos_map now keys on (asset_class, symbol); a same-symbol cross-asset-class book is no longer collapsed into one cap bucket. _portfolio_cap_clip signature unchanged (deterministic_equity reuse safe); cr04/cr05 not regressed; flag-OFF byte-identical.

title: write_snapshot + write_sector_median corrupt-parquet branch silently TRUNCATES all historical PIT rows: a read error resets existing to empty, then atomic-renames one row over the file
description:
VERIFIED (cs59 concurrent critique). fundamentals_provider.py write_snapshot (~:533-542) and write_sector_median (~:570-576): on pd.read_parquet(path) RAISING (transient/torn/corrupt read), `existing` is reset to an EMPTY DataFrame, then `merged` (= just the one new row) is _atomic_write_parquet'd over the file — the ENTIRE historical point-in-time series for that ticker/sector is irrecoverably destroyed. Same write-side PIT-history-mutation class as cs42(b)/cs59, but triggered by a READ ERROR rather than a re-fetch, and it is a SILENT FAILURE (only a logger.warning) + fail-open data-loss (money-software must fail-CLOSED). FIX: QUARANTINE the corrupt file (rename .corrupt) before starting fresh, OR RAISE so the operator notices, rather than silently truncating history. Scope: data/fundamentals_provider.py only (both write paths). Sibling of cs42(b)/cs59 (write-side PIT) + the silent-failure/fail-open family (cr05). NEW (cs59 critique).

title: asof-validation fold asymmetry: _apply_execution_unsafe rejects future-bound/unparseable asof_execution but _replay_record (rebuild) has NO guard — reconstruct_from folds a poisoned record the live incremental book dropped
description:

title: cached_fetch cs58 _calendar_bound learns only RECURRING gaps (count>=2), so a market HOLIDAY (Fri->Tue=4d, recurs <2x) extends the right-edge gap beyond the learned weekend bound -> a fresh cache MISSes+refetches when --end anchors the first session after a holiday
description:
VERIFIED (cs58 concurrent critique). cs58 (MERGED) fixed the cs43 regression for the COMMON case by learning the cache's own RECURRING inter-bar gap (_calendar_bound, count>=2 -> the weekend/overnight rhythm). But a market HOLIDAY produces a NON-recurring (or rarely-recurring) longer trailing gap: a Friday close before a Monday holiday, with --end anchored the Tuesday after, sits Fri->Tue = 4 calendar days > the learned 3-day weekend bound, and a single holiday recurs <2x in a typical backtest window -> the >=2 recurrence gate does not learn it -> the fresh fully-supplied cache MISSes + refetches on EVERY run (the same refetch-forever shape cs58 fixed for weekends), when --end anchors the first session after a holiday. P2 (narrower than cs58's P1 weekend case — holidays are ~9/year vs 52 weekends, and only bite when --end lands exactly on the post-holiday session). FIX OPTIONS: (A) drop the >=2 recurrence gate and use the cache's LARGEST trailing inter-bar gap (or max observed in-cache gap) as the edge bound, while keeping the cs50 contiguity check on the SEPARATE canonical bound so an interior one-off hole still fails (the cs58 prove's option A, deferred); (B) a small holiday-calendar awareness (a trading-calendar lib) — heavier. Prefer (A). Must keep cs43 multi-month MISS + cs50 interior-hole MISS + cutoff=None byte-identical. Scope: data/cache.py only. NEW (cs58 critique).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit b0093c0). cached_fetch now splits the bounds: the recurrence-based _calendar_bound gates ONLY the cs50 contiguity check, while the right-edge freshness gate uses a looser _edge_bound (_calendar_bound + one closed-session-day holiday allowance), so a non-recurring market holiday (Fri->Tue=4d) at the edge no longer refetch-loops. cs58 weekend HIT, cs43 multi-month MISS, cs50 interior-hole MISS, cs49 short-circuit, cutoff=None byte-identical all preserved. 35 tests.

title: FillDeltaNormalizer._bucket resolves the running-net account with bare rec.get('account_id') instead of cs52 _resolve_account — rebuild fold collapses reactor_metadata-only accounts (alpaca-paper) into paper-default while the incremental fold reads per-account net (flag-ON DELTA_NORMALIZER divergence)
description:
VERIFIED (review-team pass-2, empirical repro). A 6TH fold-divergence axis (cs44/cs51/cs52/cs57 fixed the folds, cs62 asof in-flight): cs52's account-resolution fix was applied to BOTH folds' BOOKING grain but NOT to the FillDeltaNormalizer's internal running-net bucket. Under HERMES_QUANT_DELTA_NORMALIZER=1 the rebuild fold (reconstruct_from -> FillDeltaNormalizer.delta_for -> _bucket, fill_delta_normalizer.py:46-51) keys the carry-forward running-net on the BARE top-level account_id, but the persisted log serializes account_id ONLY inside reactor_metadata, so _bucket returns 'paper-default' for an alpaca-paper fill while the incremental fold (apply_execution, acct=_resolve_account -> reads old_qty WHERE account_id=acct) reads the per-account net. delta = target - running_net therefore DIFFERS between folds: the rebuild collapses every reactor_metadata-only account onto one paper-default bucket. The two books diverge on the gate-sized NAV when >1 named account shares a symbol. EMPIRICAL: rec with reactor_metadata.account_id='alpaca-paper' -> _bucket[0]=='paper-default' but _resolve_account=='alpaca-paper' (DIVERGENT, reproduced). DISTINCT from ms1 (schema-mix seeding) + ra01 (resolved inflation symptom). Flag default-OFF byte-identical (_bucket unreachable when normalizer off). FIX: have _bucket call _resolve_account (or its identical inline) so the normalizer's running-net partition matches the fold's booking partition. Scope: fill_delta_normalizer.py only (single helper). NEW (review-team pass-2 wb1zsz2na). FILE-DISJOINT from cs60/61/62/63/56 in-flight.

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 25d421a). FillDeltaNormalizer._bucket now resolves the account via an inlined _resolve_account (top-level account_id -> reactor_metadata.account_id -> paper-default, byte-for-byte with cs52) so the normalizer's running-net partition matches the booking fold's; was: bare top-level account_id collapsed reactor_metadata-only accounts (alpaca-paper) into paper-default under DELTA_NORMALIZER=1. title: OHLCV parquet cache (data/cache.py) silently OVERWRITES a historical bar on re-fetch: normalize_bars drop_duplicates(keep='last') + append read-concat-rewrite, no fetched_at column — a vendor restatement / split re-adjustment / late print rewrites cached history, so a backtest replayed at the same --end reads a DIFFERENT past price
description:
VERIFIED (review-team pass-2, empirical repro 100->50 silent overwrite). A 5TH PIT instance OUTSIDE the four guarded fundamentals sites (cs42b/cs53/cs59/cs61): the OHLCV time-series cache has the SAME re-fetch-rewrites-history defect cs42b/cs59 closed on the fundamentals side but was never given the PIT-preserving dedup. write_snapshot carries a fetched_at column + a _same_day ranking (same-day-correction-wins, cross-day-backfill-loses); the OHLCV schema [timestamp,open,high,low,close,volume] (cache.py:419) has NO fetched_at, so normalize_bars (cache.py:428) does a bare drop_duplicates(subset=['timestamp'],keep='last') and append (cache.py:194-199) read-concats incoming AFTER existing then rewrites — so a re-fetch returning a revised value for a PAST timestamp (vendor restatement, split/dividend re-adjustment, late print, differently-sized window) silently OVERWRITES the cached historical bar with no immutability/first-write-wins guard and no test. CRITICALLY DISTINCT from the entire cs38/cs43/cs49/cs50/cs58/cs63 cache family, which ALL bound the SERVED WINDOW (future-bars, right-edge staleness, contiguity, calendar-gap) — none guards interior value-rewrite on re-fetch. A backtest replayed at the same --end after such a re-fetch reads a different historical price -> non-reproducible OOS metrics the promotion gate trusts. NOT a forward-lookahead leak (cs38 cutoff handles future bars); a PIT-REPRODUCIBILITY gap -> P2. FIX: add a fetched_at column to the OHLCV schema + apply the cs59-style same-day-correction-wins / cross-day-backfill-loses dedup so a cross-day re-fetch cannot overwrite a historical bar; add a first-write-immutability test. Scope: data/cache.py (+ a cache-parquet schema migration — re-invoke schema-migration-safety, but the OHLCV parquet is a derived CACHE, regenerable, NOT state.db, so lower risk). NEW (review-team pass-2). COLLISION NOTE: cache.py — cs63 IN-FLIGHT there; SEQUENCE cs66 AFTER cs63 merges.

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 22cd76c). The OHLCV cache now carries an INTERNAL fetched_at storage column (7-col on-disk frame; normalize_bars stays the 6-col SERVED normalizer so consumers are byte-identical, no fetched_at leak) + the cs59-mirror PIT dedup keyed on the bar timestamp (same-day correction wins, cross-day backfill loses). Legacy fetched_at-less files backfill a sentinel on read (idempotent migration; the OHLCV parquet/csv is a DERIVED regenerable cache, not state.db). First-write + same-day-correction + served-window (cs38/43/49/50/58/63) behavior all byte-identical. 6 cs66 tests + 41 cache tests green. Closes the 5th + final PIT-integrity instance. Salvaged-by-refire (the lane died after Prove on the first run).

title: refresh() returns skipped:fresh forever on a future fetched_at — read_latest(as_of=None) max-fetched_at row yields negative age_h < ttl, starving the cron's refresh
description:
VERIFIED (cs61 concurrent critique, empirical repro). fundamentals_provider.py:622-627 refresh() computes age_h from read_latest(ticker) with as_of=None, which sorts by fetched_at and returns the MAX-fetched_at row. A cached row whose fetched_at is in the FUTURE relative to the cron wall-clock (NTP/clock-skew regression, container clock jump, a fabricated/corrupt parquet, or a backfill tool stamping a future timestamp) makes age_h NEGATIVE, so `age_h < self.ttl_hours` is True and the ticker is returned 'skipped:fresh' — PERMANENTLY, until wall-clock advances past that timestamp. The ticker's fundamentals silently go stale and are never re-fetched (silence-by-default AVAILABILITY degradation in money-software). PROVEN: a row stamped fetched_at=now+2d -> age_h=-48.0; refresh(['AAPL']) -> {'AAPL':'skipped:fresh'}. SAME future-timestamp class as cs42(a)/cs53 (a future fetched_at defeats a staleness/age gate) but on the COLD REFRESH path, which has NO guard — the cs42(a)/cs53 guards are scoped to the as_of-is-not-None READ path; test_cs42_no_as_of_latest_path_untouched documents the as_of=None read returning the future row as intentional WITHOUT considering this second-order refresh-starvation. FIX: in refresh(), treat fetched_at > now as max-stale / force-refresh (clamp age_h, or guard fetched_at <= now) rather than fresh. Scope: data/fundamentals_provider.py only. Sibling of cs42a/cs53/cs59/cs61 (the fundamentals future-timestamp/PIT family). NEW (cs61 critique).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit ebb484b). refresh() now gates freshness on 0 <= age_h < ttl_hours, so a future-stamped fetched_at (negative age_h) is treated max-stale and force-refreshed instead of skipped:fresh-forever; a genuinely-fresh past stamp byte-identical. Cold-refresh sibling of the cs42a/cs53 read-path future-fetch guards. 45 tests green. Salvaged from the in-flight lane, orchestrator-reviewed.

title: read_sector_median_pe as_of=None LIVE path accepts a FUTURE-fetched median: cs53's fetched_at<=as_of guard is scoped to as_of!=None, so the live pe_relative denominator (asof_ts=now) has no future-fetch guard — a negative age_days defeats the 30d staleness gate
description:
VERIFIED (cs67 concurrent critique, empirically reproduced, code-confirmed at fundamentals_provider.py:536-543). cs53 (MERGED) added the fetched_at<=as_of future-fetch guard to read_sector_median_pe but SCOPED it `if as_of is not None:` (the point-in-time backtest read). On the as_of=None LIVE read path (asof_ts defaults to now) — the path the LIVE FundamentalsAnalyst uses for the pe_relative DENOMINATOR — that drop is SKIPPED, so a sector-median row with as_of_date=today + fetched_at=now+10d survives, age_days=(now-(now+10d)).days=-10, and the staleness gate `age_days > SECTOR_MEDIAN_STALE_HARD_DAYS (30)` is False for the negative value -> the future-fetched median is ACCEPTED as fresh (returned 22.0) instead of abstaining. A clock-skew/corrupt/backfill future stamp on the denominator silently feeds a not-yet-knowable sector median into the live pe_relative sub-signal (an ADR-0004 gate input). P1: LIVE money-state gate input, not a backtest-only path. EXACTLY the path-scoping-gap class as cs67 (a guard scoped to one call path leaves the sibling path exposed). FIX: clamp negative age_days to max-stale (return None / abstain) OR drop fetched_at>asof_ts on the as_of=None path too — symmetric with the cs67 refresh clamp; do NOT change the as_of!=None path (cs53, correct). Scope: data/fundamentals_provider.py read_sector_median_pe only. Sibling of cs53/cs67/cs42a. NEW (cs67 critique).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit dd4b6b3). read_sector_median_pe staleness gate now clamps a NEGATIVE age_days (`if age_days < 0 or age_days > HARD_DAYS: return None`), so on the as_of=None LIVE path (where cs53's fetched_at<=as_of drop is skipped) a future-fetched median (negative age) abstains instead of being accepted as fresh into the live pe_relative denominator. PIT path (cs53, as_of!=None) byte-identical (the clamp is a dead no-op there — cs53 already drops future fetched_at so age_days>=0). 52 tests green.

title: refresh_sector_medians stamps the median as_of_date/fetched_at=now from STALE constituent reads (no per-constituent freshness check) — a months-stale denominator masquerades as fresh through the 30d gate
description:
VERIFIED (cs67 concurrent critique, empirically reproduced). refresh_sector_medians (fundamentals_provider.py:699-742) builds the sector median from read_latest(ticker, as_of=None) for each constituent, then writes the median row stamped as_of_date=now.normalize() / fetched_at=now — with NO check that the constituent snapshots are themselves fresh. Empirical: two constituents whose only snapshots are ~5 months stale (fetched 2026-01-01) still produce out={'Tech':{'n':2,'median_pe':15.0}} + a sector-median row stamped TODAY. That fresh today-stamp then sails through read_sector_median_pe's 30d hard-staleness gate (which measures the MEDIAN-ROW fetched_at, NOT constituent age), so the analyst treats a months-stale denominator as fresh. Money-software: stale fundamentals masquerade as fresh in the pe_relative denominator (an ADR-0004 gate input). DISTINCT from cs59 (median write PIT-preservation) + cs53/cs68 (median read future-fetch) — this is the median's OWN freshness derived from constituent freshness. FIX: skip/down-weight constituents whose read_latest fetched_at age exceeds a freshness bound (reuse ttl_hours or a sector-constituent staleness day-bound) before taking the median, OR stamp the median's effective age from the OLDEST contributing constituent (so the 30d gate sees the true staleness). Scope: data/fundamentals_provider.py refresh_sector_medians only. Sibling of cs67 (silent-stale). NEW (cs67 critique).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit dd4b6b3). refresh_sector_medians now skips a constituent whose read_latest fetched_at age is negative (future) or > SECTOR_MEDIAN_STALE_HARD_DAYS before taking the median, so the written median is genuinely fresh and the 30d read gate keeps measuring true freshness; an all-stale sector writes no row (silence-by-default). Chose SKIP over backdating (backdating would collide with the cs59 _same_day dedup); read_latest semantics unchanged (cs42a untouched). Fresh-constituent sector byte-identical.

title: OHLCV cache dual-format divergence: write() can degrade a re-fetch to .csv but never invalidates the stale .parquet, and read()/path prefer the .parquet — an env with the parquet engine silently serves OLD bars and drops the fresh CSV re-fetch
description:
VERIFIED (cs66 concurrent critique, empirically reproduced). Same PIT-reproducibility/faithfulness class as cs66 but a DISTINCT root cause (dual-format source-of-truth ambiguity, not the dedup/append schema). OhlcvCache.write() can degrade a re-fetch to .csv (cache.py:238-242, e.g. when the parquet engine is unavailable at write time) but NEVER invalidates a pre-existing stale .parquet for the same stem; and path/read() (cache.py:209-227) PREFER the .parquet when prefer_parquet and it exists. So a backtest replayed in an environment where the parquet engine IS available silently serves the OLD .parquet bars and DROPS the fresh CSV re-fetch — environment-dependent non-reproducibility (the same --end yields different bars depending on which format the runtime can read). FIX: on write, if a sibling format file exists for the same stem, either write BOTH formats or DELETE/invalidate the not-written one so there is a single source of truth; OR make read() prefer the NEWEST-mtime format. Scope: data/cache.py only. Sibling of cs66 (OHLCV PIT). NEW (cs66 critique).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 726b1cd). OHLCV cache now guarantees a single source of truth: `path` prefers the NEWEST-mtime format when both .parquet+.csv exist (heals already-divergent/legacy caches, later write wins, byte-identical when one format), AND write/_write_storage delete the other-format sibling after a successful write (durable). read() keeps the cs61 parquet->csv engine-absent/corrupt fallback; cs66 fetched_at storage column survives both formats; cs38/43/49/50/58/63 served-window family + normalize_bars untouched. Single-format byte-identical. 47 cache tests green.

title: cached_fetch MISS-path discards an interior-gap BACKFILL when the fetch does not advance the right edge (cs49 churn-skip over-fires): refetch-forever + permanently-discontiguous served window
description:
VERIFIED (cs66-refire concurrent critique, empirically reproduced, code-confirmed at cache.py:595-613). cs49 (MERGED) added the `fetched_advances` churn-skip: on a MISS, if the just-fetched window's newest at-or-before-cutoff bar does NOT exceed the pre-fetch eligible right edge (pre_fetch_max), fetched_advances=False -> line 612 `merged = cached` and `cache.append(fetched)` is SKIPPED (cache.py:604-613). cs49 reasoned ONLY about the RIGHT EDGE (a delisted/lagging provider re-serving the same stale tail -> avoid the append churn). But the guard ALSO discards a fetch that BACKFILLS an INTERIOR hole below the cutoff without advancing the edge — which is EXACTLY the data the cs50 contiguity gate demands the provider supply. EMPIRICAL: cache=[2026-01-01,02,10] (close 100,101,110), cutoff=2026-01-10. A fetch returning the missing interior bars 03..09 (no bar past day 10) sets fetched_advances=False, so cache.append is SKIPPED: the persisted cache stays [100,101,110] and the served window stays the discontiguous [100,101,110]. Across 3 identical replays at the same cutoff fetch_fn is called 3x (REFETCH-FOREVER) and the served window is NEVER repaired — the cs50 HIT gate keeps rejecting it on every run because the interior hole is never persisted. CONTROL: when the fetch ALSO advances the edge (cutoff=2026-01-11, fetch 03..11) the append runs and the cache becomes contiguous [100..110] — proving the defect is scoped to the NON-ADVANCING interior backfill. A genuine INTERACTION bug between cs49 (churn-skip, guards only the edge) and cs50 (contiguity gate, detects but cannot persist the fix). DISTINCT from cs49/cs50/cs58/cs63/cs66. FIX: the fetched_advances churn-skip must ALSO append when the fetch backfills a NEW interior bar the cache lacked (not just when it advances the right edge) — e.g. append when fetched contains any timestamp not already in cached (a genuine new bar, edge OR interior), while still skipping a pure no-new-data re-serve (the cs49 churn case). Must keep cs49's refetch-forever fix for the stale-edge case + cs50 contiguity + cs66 PIT dedup + cutoff=None byte-identical. Scope: data/cache.py only. NEW (cs66-refire critique). NOTE: cache.py has a lane (cs70 dual-format) IN-FLIGHT — SEQUENCE cs71 after cs70 merges (same file).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 11ac675). the cs49 fetched_advances churn-skip now appends when the fetch contains ANY new timestamp (fetched_has_new, edge OR interior), not just when it advances the right edge — so an interior backfill is persisted in one fetch (contiguous served window, no refetch loop). The cs49 stale-edge NO-new-data case still skips (no churn). cs50 contiguity gate + right_edge_stale_days + cs66 dedup + cs70 single-source + cutoff=None all unchanged. 51 cache tests green.

title: OHLCV cache stem collision: _safe_component lossily maps distinct provider/symbol identities to the SAME cache file (BTC/USDT and BTC:USDT both -> BTC_USDT)
description:
VERIFIED (cs70 concurrent critique, code-confirmed cache.py:685-688). _safe_component collapses '/', ':', and any non-[A-Za-z0-9_.-] char to '_', so DISTINCT identities share one cache stem: _safe_component('ccxt:binance')=='ccxt_binance' (provider-dir collision); _safe_component('BTC/USDT')==_safe_component('BTC:USDT')=='BTC_USDT', and any 'BTC/USDT' collides with a literal 'BTC_USDT' -> cache stem 'BTC_USDT-1h'. In production cli/__init__.py:1759-1771 the provider arrives as 'ccxt:<exchange>' and the symbol as a ccxt BASE/QUOTE pair, so two instruments differing only by separator silently MERGE into one cache file -> blended/wrong OHLCV bars served with NO signal -> a backtest reads prices for the WRONG instrument (a PIT/reproducibility + cross-contamination hazard, same charter-invariant class as cs66/cs70). Empirically reproduced: _safe_component('BTC/USDT')=='BTC_USDT', cache stem identical to a literal BTC_USDT. NOT covered by any seed (cs51 OCC per-leg dedup / cs44 double-book / cs65 multileg pos_map are different sanitize/collision sites). FIX: make the sanitizer INJECTIVE — encode the lossy chars distinctly (percent/hex-escape '/' and ':' rather than collapse both to '_'), OR hash-suffix the raw identity into the stem so distinct symbols can never share a file. Narrow trigger (separator-only overlap on one provider) but a real cross-instrument contamination of the gate-fed cache. Scope: data/cache.py only. Sibling of cs66/cs70 (cache PIT/faithfulness). NEW (cs70 critique). SEQUENCE with cs71 (both cache.py) — bundle.

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 11ac675). _safe_component is now INJECTIVE: an already-safe component (no non-[A-Za-z0-9_.-] char) is returned byte-identical; a component containing an unsafe char percent-escapes each offending char per UTF-8 byte, so '/' and ':' yield DISTINCT stems and BTC/USDT vs BTC:USDT vs literal BTC_USDT can never share a cache file (was: all collapsed to BTC_USDT -> blended OHLCV for the wrong instrument). Existing safe caches not orphaned. 51 cache tests green.

title: cached_fetch MISS-path serves a DISCONTIGUOUS lookback window with NO contiguity guard + NO honesty flag when the provider advances the right edge but cannot backfill an UNFILLABLE interior hole (delisted/short-window/downtime)
description:
VERIFIED (cs7172 concurrent critique). DISTINCT from cs71 (which heals a FILLABLE interior hole by persisting the backfill) and cs50 (the HIT-path contiguity gate). On the MISS path, when the provider ADVANCES the right edge (so the append runs + fetched_advances=True) but CANNOT backfill a genuinely-UNFILLABLE interior hole (a delisted stretch, a provider short-window, an exchange-downtime gap the provider will never return), the served lookback tail GLUES bars across the unfillable interior hole with NO contiguity guard and NO honesty flag (the cs50 contiguity check is on the HIT path; the MISS path serves whatever the merged tail is). A backtest then computes returns/indicators across the hole -> a spurious seam return, with no right_edge_stale_days-style signal telling the caller the window is internally discontiguous. cs49's right_edge_stale_days flags a stale EDGE; there is no analogous interior-discontiguity flag on the MISS path. FIX: on the MISS path, after the append+tail, when cutoff is set, check the SERVED window's max interior inter-bar gap (reuse the cs50 contig_bound) and either emit an honesty flag (e.g. meta['interior_gap_days']) so the caller can ABSTAIN, or refuse to serve a discontiguous window — symmetric with the cs49 right_edge_stale_days honesty signal. Distinguish a genuinely-unfillable hole (don't refetch-forever — that's the cs71 boundary) from a fillable one (cs71 heals). Scope: data/cache.py only. Sibling of cs49/cs50/cs71. NEW (cs7172 critique).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 5838f71). cached_fetch MISS-path now emits meta['interior_gap_days'] + meta['served_window_discontiguous'] (reusing the cs50 _calendar_bound contig_bound, *1.5 tolerance) when the served window's max interior inter-bar gap exceeds the bound — the interior-axis analog of cs49's right_edge_stale_days, so the caller can ABSTAIN on an unfillable-interior-hole window. Flag-only (no refetch — cs71's append already ran on the edge-advance; no refuse-to-serve); a FILLABLE hole is still healed by cs71 (no flag); contiguous served window + cutoff=None byte-identical; HIT path + cs38/43/49/50/58/63/66/70/71/72 intact. 57 cache tests green. cs73's concurrent critique returned ZERO new candidates -> the cache.py serve-path correctness/honesty matrix (future-prune/edge-staleness/HIT-contiguity/interior-heal/interior-flag/value-PIT/dual-format/stem-injectivity) is COMPLETE.

title: cached_fetch cs50 HIT-path contiguity gate refetch-loops a FRESH-edge SHORT cache over a single non-recurring weekend/overnight session gap (the cs63/cs73 widening was applied to _edge_bound + the MISS flag but NOT the HIT gate)
description:
VERIFIED + empirically reproduced (convergence-check review wve6632zd). cache.py:644 sets the cs50 HIT contiguity bound contig_bound = _calendar_bound(bound, eligible['timestamp']) — the RECURRENCE-ONLY bound (a gap must appear >=2x to be learned, cache.py:150 counts[counts>=2]). For a SHORT cache whose entire eligible set straddles exactly ONE legitimate weekend (or one overnight session gap), the weekend occurs only once -> _calendar_bound degrades to the canonical 1-step floor (1d). At cache.py:649-652 the served tail's max_gap (3d weekend) exceeds contig_bound*1.5 (1.5d) -> contiguous=False -> the HIT is REJECTED at :653 EVEN THOUGH the right edge is PERFECTLY FRESH (cutoff==newest, edge_bound=2d, fresh_right_edge=True at :646). The MISS path re-serves the identical bars, cs49/cs71 correctly skip the append (mtime stable), BUT fetch_fn() at :670 is CALLED on EVERY replay = refetch-forever (the calls==0 contract). RED: a 10-bar Mon-Fri daily cache (one weekend) fresh edge, 3 replays -> hits=[F,F,F], calls=3; CONTROL: a 20-bar 4-week cache (weekend RECURS) HITs calls=0; INTRADAY 14-bar 1h one-overnight-gap likewise calls=3. DISTINCT from cs58 (STALE edge, no calls==0 assertion), cs63 (widened ONLY _edge_bound + deliberately kept the gate on the tighter _calendar_bound — silently assumes the weekend RECURS, fails for any <=2-trading-week cache), cs73 (fixed only the MISS-path FLAG to learn from the broad merged set; the HIT GATE at :644 still learns from the short eligible set — the exact asymmetry cs73's own comment warns about, applied to the GATE not the FLAG). PRODUCTION-REACHABLE: cli/__init__.py:1759 cached_fetch(cutoff=as_of, no max_staleness); a short --lookback or a newly-listed/thin symbol yields a 1-2 trading-week cache that re-fetches the real provider on every same---end replay. FIX (mirror cs63 spirit on the HIT gate): give the contiguity bound a single-closed-session-day tolerance from the cache's own largest OBSERVED gap (not recurrence-only), e.g. contig_bound = max(_calendar_bound(...), <one-session tolerance>) — so one legitimate session gap in a short cache passes while a cs50 multi-step interior hole (many session-days) still fails. Scope: data/cache.py only. NEW (convergence-check wve6632zd).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 85019f7). cached_fetch HIT contiguity gate now uses _edge_bound (the cs63 holiday-tolerant bound) instead of recurrence-only _calendar_bound, so a short single-weekend/overnight fresh-edge cache HITs (no refetch-forever). One-line change (contig_bound = edge_bound). cs50 multi-step interior-hole rejection + cs43 multi-month edge + cs58 + cs73 MISS-flag preserved; recurring-weekend + cutoff=None byte-identical. 62 cache tests green.

title: read_sector_median_pe as_of=None staleness gate (cs68) accepts a NaT/missing fetched_at as fresh — NaN defeats both the `<0` and `>HARD` comparisons (fail-OPEN; the lone NaN-unsafe clamp vs NaN-safe cs67/cs69 siblings)
description:
VERIFIED + empirically reproduced (convergence-check review wve6632zd). fundamentals_provider.py:542 age_days = (asof_ts - pd.Timestamp(latest['fetched_at'])).days; when the surviving latest sector-median row has fetched_at=NaT (corrupt/torn/hand-built parquet, old-schema migration, a backfill omitting the stamp) age_days is float('nan'). The cs68 guard at :557 `if age_days < 0 or age_days > SECTOR_MEDIAN_STALE_HARD_DAYS: return None` evaluates `nan<0`->False and `nan>30`->False, so the 30d HARD gate is BYPASSED and the median (the pe_relative DENOMINATOR) is silently ACCEPTED as fresh despite no knowable fetch time — fail-OPEN, violating silence-by-default. DISTINCT from cs68 (which closed only the NEGATIVE-age future-fetch case on the same as_of=None path); the NaN/NaT case falls through the SAME gate. It is the LONE NaN-unsafe clamp of the family: cs67 (:714) uses bounded-below `if 0 <= age_h < ttl` (NaN-safe), cs69 (:761) has an explicit `pd.isna(fetched_at): continue` pre-guard (NaN-safe). LATENT today (priority 3): the sole live caller analysts/fundamentals.py:523 passes as_of=ctx.asof (NEVER None), and on the as_of!=None PIT path cs53 (:536-539 df=df[df['fetched_at']<=asof_ts]) drops a NaT row upstream (NaT comparisons False) -> returns None correctly; the gap bites only the as_of=None LIVE path (today exercised by tests + the cs68 defended live-honesty contract; live if a future caller uses the as_of=None read). RED: a Tech sector-median row as_of_date=2026-01-01 + fetched_at=NaT + median_pe=22.0, lag flag OFF -> read_sector_median_pe('Tech') (as_of=None) returns 22.0 (fail-OPEN). FIX (same one-line spirit as cs67): bound below + reject NaN, e.g. `if not (0 <= age_days <= SECTOR_MEDIAN_STALE_HARD_DAYS): return None` — symmetric with cs67/cs69, silence-by-default; the genuinely-fresh past-stamp case [0,30] stays byte-identical. Scope: data/fundamentals_provider.py only. NEW (convergence-check wve6632zd).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 6b5d616). read_sector_median_pe staleness clamp is now NaN-safe: `if not (0 <= age_days <= SECTOR_MEDIAN_STALE_HARD_DAYS): return None` (mirrors cs67), so a NaT fetched_at (nan age) abstains instead of being accepted as fresh (was fail-OPEN — nan defeats both `<0` and `>HARD`). LATENT (the live caller passes as_of!=None where cs53 drops NaT upstream; bites only the as_of=None read). cs53/cs67/cs69 untouched; fresh-past + PIT byte-identical. 53 tests green.

title: cs73 MISS-path interior-discontiguity FLAG uses recurrence-only _calendar_bound over merged — false-fires on a SHORT cache straddling exactly ONE weekend (the symmetric MISS-side twin of cs74, not fixed by cs74's HIT-path scope)
description:
VERIFIED + empirically reproduced (cs74 concurrent critique). cache.py:781 (post-cs74) computes the cs73 MISS-path interior-discontiguity bound as `contig_bound = _calendar_bound(bound, merged['timestamp'])` — the RECURRENCE-ONLY bound (cache.py:150 counts[counts>=2]). cs73's author moved the learning source from the short served tail to the BROAD merged set to dodge a false-flag, but that defense only works when merged ITSELF contains the weekend gap >=2x. For a SHORT cache whose ENTIRE merged set straddles exactly ONE legitimate weekend (or one overnight session), the weekend appears only ONCE even in merged -> _calendar_bound degrades to the 1-step floor -> a 3d weekend exceeds bound*1.5 -> meta['served_window_discontiguous']=True + meta['interior_gap_days'] set on a PERFECTLY-CONTIGUOUS-modulo-weekends short window -> the caller may wrongly ABSTAIN on a legitimate short cache. The SYMMETRIC MISS-side twin of cs74 (which fixed the HIT GATE by switching to _edge_bound); cs74's scope was HIT-path-only so the MISS-path flag still has the bug. FIX: mirror cs74 — the cs73 MISS-path flag bound should also use _edge_bound (the cs63 holiday-tolerant bound) so one legitimate session gap does not false-flag, while a genuinely-unfillable multi-step interior hole (many session-days) STILL flags. Scope: data/cache.py only (the :781 contig_bound for the MISS flag). NEW (cs74 critique).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 9884704). The cs73 MISS-path interior-discontiguity flag now uses _edge_bound (the cs63 holiday-tolerant bound) instead of recurrence-only _calendar_bound, so a short single-weekend cache no longer false-flags served_window_discontiguous; cs73's genuinely-unfillable multi-step interior hole STILL flags; recurring-weekend + cutoff=None byte-identical. One-line change mirroring cs74. COMPLETES the contiguity family: all 3 bounds (edge cs63, HIT gate cs74, MISS flag cs76) now use _edge_bound. 66 cache tests green.

title: FundamentalsAnalyst._fetch_fundamentals datum-staleness gate is fail-OPEN on a FUTURE-dated period_end/report_date: datum_age_days = (asof - basis).days with only a `> HARD_LIMIT` upper-bound check accepts a negative (future-basis) age
description:
VERIFIED (cs75 concurrent critique, code-confirmed). Same fail-OPEN-on-future-timestamp / no-lookahead class as cs42a/cs53/cs67/cs68/cs69/cs75 but a NEW axis (the analyst's DATUM-recency basis = period_end/report_date) + a NEW file (analysts/fundamentals.py, an immediate provider collaborator). analysts/fundamentals.py:277 `datum_age_days = (asof - basis).days` then :278 `if datum_age_days > self._STALENESS_DATUM_DAYS_HARD_LIMIT: return None` — there is NO lower-bound / future-basis guard (grep confirms the only datum_age check is the `> HARD_LIMIT` one). basis is the report_date/period_end of the fundamentals datum; a FUTURE-dated basis (corrupt/hand-built/backfilled period_end, or a vendor mis-stamp) makes datum_age_days NEGATIVE, and `negative > HARD_LIMIT` is False -> the gate is BYPASSED -> a not-yet-knowable fundamental datum is scored as a current datum (reachable on the reporting-lag-flag-OFF path; the cs12 lag filter is the other guard but is flag-gated). FIX: bound below + reject NaN, mirroring cs67/cs75: `if not (0 <= datum_age_days <= self._STALENESS_DATUM_DAYS_HARD_LIMIT): return None`. The genuinely-current datum case [0,HARD] byte-identical. Scope: analysts/fundamentals.py only (DISJOINT from the fundamentals_provider.py family). Sibling of cs68/cs75 (the future-timestamp/staleness family, analyst axis). NEW (cs75 critique).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 2650e02). _fetch_fundamentals datum-staleness gate is now bounded-below + NaN-safe: `if not (0 <= datum_age_days <= _STALENESS_DATUM_DAYS_HARD_LIMIT): return None` (mirrors cs75), so a future-dated period_end/report_date (negative age) or NaN-derived age abstains instead of being scored as current. Current datum [0,190] byte-identical; the basis-less fetched_at fallback + cs40 two-axis gate + cs45/cs47 abstain + cs12 lag all untouched. 26 analyst tests green.

title: FundamentalsAnalyst fetched_at-fallback staleness gate is fail-OPEN on a future/NaT fetched_at (fundamentals.py:302 bare `> HARD_LIMIT`, no lower bound, not NaN-safe) — the last unbounded sibling gate in the file (defended upstream by cs42a)
description:
VERIFIED (cs77 concurrent critique, math-confirmed). analysts/fundamentals.py:302 (the basis-LESS fetched_at cron-liveness fallback, taken when _datum_basis returns None — no report_date AND no period_end): `age_days = (asof - fetched_at).days` then `if age_days > self._STALENESS_FETCHED_AT_DAYS_HARD_LIMIT (7): return None`. FIX: mirror cs77/cs75 — `if not (0 <= age_days <= self._STALENESS_FETCHED_AT_DAYS_HARD_LIMIT): return None`. A genuinely-fresh fetched_at [0,7] byte-identical. Scope: analysts/fundamentals.py only. Sibling of cs77 (same file, fetched_at axis). NEW (cs77 critique). NOTE: same file as cs77 — sequence after cs77 merges (DONE: 2650e02).

|| RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 231b202). The basis-less fetched_at cron-liveness fallback gate is now bounded-below + NaN-safe: `if not (0 <= age_days <= _STALENESS_FETCHED_AT_DAYS_HARD_LIMIT): return None` (mirrors cs77/cs75), so a future fetched_at (negative age) or NaT-value fetched_at (nan age) abstains instead of being scored as fresh. Genuinely-fresh [0,7] byte-identical; the datum-axis gate (cs77), cs40 two-axis split, cs45/cs47 untouched. COMPLETES the future-timestamp/staleness family: every staleness gate (provider cs42a/53/67/68/75 + analyst datum cs77 + analyst fetched_at cs78) is bounded-below + NaN-safe. cs78's concurrent critique returned ZERO genuinely-new findings -> the family is symmetry-closed. 29 analyst tests green.

title: cached_fetch raises TypeError on a tz-NAIVE cutoff (no tz-normalization of the cutoff arg) — DEFERRED: not live-reachable (sole caller tz-localizes as_of), a robustness-hardening nicety
description:
VERIFIED (cs76 concurrent critique, empirically reproduced): passing a tz-NAIVE cutoff to cached_fetch raises `TypeError: Invalid comparison between dtype=datetime64[ns, UTC] and Timestamp` at cache.py:613 `eligible = cached[cached['timestamp'] <= cutoff]` (and the :696/:715 comparisons) — cached timestamps are tz-aware (normalize_bars UTC-normalizes) but the cutoff arg is NOT tz-normalized, unlike append() which normalizes fetched_at. || ORCHESTRATOR-CAPPED / DEFERRED (convergence decision rule, 2026-06-14): NOT launched as a fix lane because it is NOT LIVE-REACHABLE — the sole production caller cli/__init__.py:1656-1658 sets `as_of = _pd.Timestamp(end)` then `as_of = as_of.tz_localize('UTC')`, so cached_fetch always receives a tz-AWARE cutoff. This is a TypeError-on-misuse robustness-hardening nicety for a hypothetical FUTURE caller passing a naive timestamp, NOT an active money-state defect and OUTSIDE the staleness/contiguity invariant matrices (both now symmetry-complete). It does NOT keep the code-fixable frontier open. FIX-WHEN-CONVENIENT (one line, defensive): tz-normalize the cutoff at the top of cached_fetch (`if cutoff is not None and cutoff.tzinfo is None: cutoff = cutoff.tz_localize('UTC')`), mirroring the as_of normalization the caller already does. A tz-aware cutoff (the live case) byte-identical. Scope: data/cache.py only. NEW (cs76 critique, orchestrator-capped P3-deferred).

|| CLOSED 2026-06-16 (fixed on the INTEGRATION branch — the stale-base lane correctly reported not-a-defect on its base where cached_fetch had no cutoff param, but the bug IS real here): cache.py cached_fetch raised TypeError: Invalid comparison between datetime64[ns,UTC] and Timestamp on a tz-NAIVE cutoff (the :613 eligible filter + cs43/cs50/cs49/cs73 comparison sites). FIX: normalize cutoff to tz-aware UTC ONCE at the top of cached_fetch (tzinfo-None->tz_localize, aware->tz_convert; None untouched). RED-verified via git-stash (EXACT TypeError reproduces without the fix) -> GREEN 3/3 + 69 cache regression. LESSON: a worktree lane branches from a STALE base; re-verify its not-a-defect verdict against the integration HEAD.
